## Project

This is a production ERP system built with Laravel 12.

This project is actively developed.

Never redesign the architecture.

Always inspect the existing code before making changes.

Continue from the current implementation.

# Coding Rules

Always follow existing project conventions.

Never create a different folder structure.

Reuse existing:

- Models
- Services
- Controllers
- Form Requests
- Traits
- Helpers
- Blade Layouts
- Components
- DataTables
- AJAX Pattern
- Permission Pattern
- Activity Logger

Do not duplicate logic.

Do not generate placeholder code.

Always generate production-ready code.

# Database Rules

Before creating tables:

- Check existing migrations.
- Reuse tables whenever possible.
- Keep foreign keys consistent.
- Follow naming conventions.
- Never duplicate data.

Do not redesign.

Use existing Bootstrap components.

Use existing layouts.

Use existing DataTable implementation.

# Post-HRM ERP Roadmap

Source: `erp.txt` (project root). This is the full ERP build order after HRM. HRM is done — do not restart or redesign it. The modules below are NOT started yet.

## Final ERP Build Order

1. HRM — **Completed**
2. Workflow Engine — **Completed**
3. CRM — **Completed**
4. Sales — **Completed**
5. Purchase — **Completed**
6. Inventory — **Completed**
7. Product Management — **Completed** (built ahead of Sales/Purchase/Inventory per the roadmap's own dependency reasoning below — see the numerous 2026-07-31 changelog entries)
8. Accounting — **Completed**
9. Asset Management — **Completed**
10. Project Management — **Completed**
11. Document Management
12. Support
13. Budget & Finance
14. Reports & Executive Dashboard

Dependency reasoning (from erp.txt — follow this order, do not skip ahead):

- Workflow Engine comes right after HRM because Sales, Purchase, Accounting, HRM and Support all need a shared approval layer.
- CRM comes before Sales because opportunities convert into sales documents.
- Product Management must exist before Sales, Purchase and Inventory because all three transact against products.
- Inventory connects to Sales and Purchase before Accounting integration.
- Accounting comes after the transaction modules because it receives automated journal entries from them.
- Reports & Executive Dashboard is last because every other module feeds it data.

## Naming / Table Conflict Guard (read before starting any module below)

HRM already owns these table/model names. Do not reuse or collide with them:

- `bank_accounts` (Employee → BankAccount, personal salary bank details). The **Accounting** module's company/business bank accounts must use a different table, e.g. `finance_bank_accounts` or `company_bank_accounts`.
- `employee_documents` (Employee → EmployeeDocument, personal HR files). The **Document Management** module's document/content-management feature must use its own table, e.g. `documents` / `document_categories`, and may optionally reference `employee_id` for "uploaded by" without merging into `employee_documents`.
- `departments` / `designations` (Masters, used by Employee). Other modules (e.g. Project Management "Teams", Budget "Department Budget") should reference these existing tables via `department_id` FK rather than creating a second departments table.
- `attendances`, `leave_*`, `payrolls`, `salary_*`, `performance_reviews`, `expense_claims`, `employee_loans` — all HRM-owned, employee-scoped. No other module should create tables with these names.
- `employees` is the canonical staff table. Asset Management's "Employee Asset Tracking" and Project Management's "Project Teams" must FK to `employees.id`, not create a parallel staff table.
- Every future module still follows the existing `status` boolean = active/inactive convention, and a separate enum (e.g. `approval_status`) for any real workflow state — same rule HRM used for Attendance Adjustments / Leave Requests / Expense Claims / Employee Loans.

### 2026-07-28

Completed

- All 27 roadmap HRM modules (Employee Types → HR Reports)
- Departments, Designations (new Masters modules, not in original roadmap)
- Employee profile "View" modal (tabbed, read-only)
- Employee Login creation (linked Admin account)
- Employee CSV Import / Export
- HRM sidebar regrouped into parent/child menu structure
- Documentation page (static sidebar link)

Database

- Standard pattern per module: one table, `status` boolean = record active/inactive toggle (NOT a workflow state).
- Workflow-style modules (Attendance Adjustments, Leave Requests, Expense Claims, Employee Loans) use a separate `approval_status` enum (pending/approved/rejected) — `status` is kept for consistency with every other module and must not be reused for workflow state.
- Master-detail pattern introduced for Salary Structures (`salary_structures` + `salary_structure_items`) and Payroll (`payrolls` + `payroll_items` snapshot).
- `employees.department` / `employees.designation` (free-text strings) were dropped and replaced with `department_id` / `designation_id` FKs to the new `departments` / `designations` tables. Any future code touching employee department/designation must use the FK + relation, not strings.
- `admins.employee_id` (nullable, unique, nullOnDelete) links a Stuff/Admin login account back to one Employee.
- All child tables (documents, contacts, bank accounts, education, experience, transfers, promotions, resignations, terminations, attendance, leave, salary, payroll, claims, loans, reviews) use `employee_id` FK with `cascadeOnDelete`.

Models

- `Employee` is the central model — holds relations to every child table plus `department()`, `designation()`, `admin()` (hasOne login account).
- Several models compute values via accessors instead of storing them: `LeaveBalance::remaining_days`, `EmployeeLoan::remaining_balance`.

Controllers / Services

- Standard CRUD modules follow Controller → Service → Model, no repository layer (matches existing project pattern).
- Transfer/Promotion services auto-apply their "to" values onto the Employee record on create (this is the intended behavior — a transfer/promotion actually changes the employee's current department/designation). After the FK migration, these now resolve Department/Designation by name instead of writing strings.
- Approval workflows (Attendance Adjustments, Leave Requests, Expense Claims, Employee Loans) each have `approve()`/`reject()` service methods; approving syncs into the related table (e.g. approved Leave Request deducts from Leave Balance; approved Attendance Adjustment updates/creates the Attendance row).
- `EmployeeController` also handles `show()` (tabbed profile), `createLogin()`/`storeLogin()`, `export()`, `importForm()`/`import()` — kept on the same controller rather than splitting, since they're all employee-scoped actions.

Views / UI

- All lookup/master modules use the existing modal (`admin.layout.app` with `'modal' => 'lg'`) + DataTables pattern.
- Employees module uses **offcanvas** instead of modal (explicit client request) — matches the Roles "Assign Permission" panel pattern (`.side-offcanvas`, `#sideForm`, `offcanvas-header/body/footer`).
- Every employee-scoped child module's index page reads `?employee_id=` from the URL to pre-filter its DataTable and shows a "Clear Filter" banner — this is the standard way to drill into one employee's records from the Employees list ("View Records" dropdown per row).
- Employee "View" modal uses Bootstrap nav-tabs inside a single `'modal' => 'xl'` — all related data is eager-loaded server-side in `EmployeeController::show()`, no per-tab AJAX.

Permissions

- Every module has `{module}.view/create/edit/delete`; approval-workflow modules add `.approve`; Payroll adds `.mark-paid` instead of `.edit` (payroll is generated/deleted, not hand-edited).
- Permission enforcement is still disabled project-wide (`dynamic_submenu.blade.php` has the `auth()->user()->can(...)` checks commented out) — permissions are seeded and ready but not yet enforced. Do not assume routes are protected by permission.

Notes

- Fixed a latent bug: `checkChildActive()` was called by `dynamic_submenu.blade.php` for menu items with children but was never defined anywhere in the codebase. It only became a real (fatal) bug once nested sidebar groups were introduced. Added the missing function to `app/Helpers/Helper.php` (global helper, autoloaded via composer `files`).
- No Excel/import package installed (`maatwebsite/excel` etc.) — CSV import/export implemented with plain PHP (`fopen`/`fputcsv`/`fgetcsv`) to avoid adding a new dependency.
- Photo/document/receipt uploads require `php artisan storage:link` to be run once per environment.

Route names get the `admin.` prefix the same way all sibling routes do.

Permissions

- Added `workflow-template.view/create/edit/delete` to `database/seeders/RolePermissionSeeder.php` under a new `// Workflow Engine` comment block, granted to `Super Admin` the same way as every other permission (via `$adminRole->givePermissionTo(Permission::all())`). Seeder code only — not executed against the live database as part of this task.

Menu

- Added `database/seeders/WorkflowMenuSeeder.php` — creates a new top-level `Module` (`slug: workflow-engine`, icon `ri-flow-chart`) with a "Workflow Engine" parent `ModuleMenu` group and "Workflow Templates" as its first child (route `admin.workflow-templates.index`), following the exact `Module`/`ModuleMenu` (`parent_id`) pattern established by `HrmMenuSeeder`. Registered in `database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php`'s `$this->call([...])` list, alongside `HrmMenuSeeder`. Seeder code only — not executed against the live database as part of this task.

Notes

- Permission enforcement remains disabled project-wide, same as every existing module — Workflow Templates routes are not protected by `can()` middleware/checks, matching current codebase behavior exactly (not a regression, not a new gap).
- Migration was run (`php artisan migrate`) since it is additive/non-destructive (creates a new table only). `RolePermissionSeeder` and `WorkflowMenuSeeder` were intentionally NOT run against the live database per task instructions — an admin must run `php artisan db:seed --class=RolePermissionSeeder` and `php artisan db:seed --class=WorkflowMenuSeeder` manually (or add permissions/menu rows through the existing Role/Module UI) to activate permissions and the sidebar entry.

Permissions

- Added `workflow-template.view/create/edit/delete` to `database/seeders/RolePermissionSeeder.php` under a new "Workflow Engine" comment section, granted to Super Admin.
- `RolePermissionSeeder` is NOT idempotent (`Permission::create` + `Role::create`, no `firstOrCreate`) — re-running it on an already-seeded DB throws a duplicate-key error. For this addition the 4 permissions were inserted directly via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto the existing "Super Admin" role instead of re-running the seeder. Future modules should do the same (or the seeder should be migrated to `updateOrCreate` — not done here to avoid touching unrelated seeder behavior).

Menus

Registered in `database/seeders/DatabaseSeeder.php` after `HrmMenuSeeder::class`. Ran once via `php artisan db:seed --class=WorkflowMenuSeeder`.

Notes

- Ran `php artisan migrate` — `2026_07_29_090000_create_workflow_templates_table` applied successfully.
- Verified end-to-end: table exists, `Module`/`ModuleMenu` rows created (module id present, group + child menu row with correct route name), `php artisan route:list --name=workflow-templates` shows all 7 routes, permissions synced to Super Admin.

Migrations + models only — no controllers/views/routes/permissions/menu for these tables in this step (they are engine-internal, managed programmatically/via the future Workflow Builder).

Database

- `workflow_definitions` — one row per module+approvable combo (`module_key` + `approvable_type` unique together), optional link to a `workflow_templates` row it was built from (`workflow_template_id`, nullOnDelete), `approval_mode` enum (single/sequential/parallel), `created_by` -> `admins.id` nullOnDelete.
- `workflow_steps` — reusable across two contexts: either belongs to a live `workflow_definition_id` (cascadeOnDelete) or to a `workflow_template_id` being edited in the builder (cascadeOnDelete); both FKs nullable, exactly one is expected to be set (enforced at the service layer when steps are written, not via DB CHECK, per existing codebase convention of app-level rather than DB-level business rules). `approval_type` enum (single/all_must_approve/any_one_approves) drives how a step's approvers must respond.
- `workflow_step_approvers` — polymorphic-by-enum approver reference (`approver_type` role/user/designation + `approver_id`), not a real FK since the target table varies by type — same pattern already used elsewhere in the codebase for approver_type-style enums (e.g. `notify_type` below) rather than true polymorphic morph columns.
- `workflow_statuses` — per-definition custom status set (`key`+`label`+`color`+`is_terminal`+`sort_order`), unique on (`workflow_definition_id`, `key`).
- `workflow_instances` — one row per approvable record's live approval run; polymorphic `approvable_type`/`approvable_id` (plain columns + index, not a morph relation column pair via `morphs()`, to match the explicit type/id column style already used for `approvable_type` on `workflow_definitions`); `resubmission_of` self-references `workflow_instances.id` (nullOnDelete) to chain resubmissions; `current_status` is a free-form string (not FK'd to `workflow_statuses.key`) so it also works before/without custom statuses being defined.
- `workflow_instance_approvals` — approval history/audit trail per instance+step, `action` enum (approved/rejected/on_hold/resubmitted/commented).
- `workflow_notification_triggers` — per-definition event->notify-target mapping (`event` enum, `notify_type` enum role/user/initiator/approver + `notify_id`), `template_message` nullable text.
- FK on-delete convention followed throughout: `cascadeOnDelete()` for required parent-owns-child FKs (matches `attendance_adjustments.employee_id`, `employee_loans.employee_id`, etc.), `nullOnDelete()` for optional/soft-linked FKs. No `restrictOnDelete()` used anywhere in this codebase, so none was introduced here either — `workflow_instances.workflow_definition_id` and `workflow_instance_approvals.workflow_step_id` use `cascadeOnDelete()`.
- Migration order: `2026_07_29_090100` through `2026_07_29_090700`, immediately after `workflow_templates` (`090000`).

Models

- `WorkflowDefinition` — belongsTo `WorkflowTemplate`, `Admin` (`createdBy`); hasMany `WorkflowStep`, `WorkflowStatus`, `WorkflowInstance`, `WorkflowNotificationTrigger`.
- `WorkflowStep` — belongsTo `WorkflowDefinition`, `WorkflowTemplate`; hasMany `WorkflowStepApprover`. Dual-parent FK constraint documented as a code comment (not a boot() rule) — no sibling model in this codebase enforces mutually-exclusive nullable FKs via boot(), so this follows existing convention rather than introducing new model-level validation machinery.
- `WorkflowStepApprover` — belongsTo `WorkflowStep`.
- `WorkflowStatus` — belongsTo `WorkflowDefinition`.
- `WorkflowInstance` — belongsTo `WorkflowDefinition`, `WorkflowStep` (`currentStep`), `Admin` (`initiatedBy`), self (`resubmissionOf`); morphTo `approvable`; hasMany `WorkflowInstanceApproval`.
- `WorkflowInstanceApproval` — belongsTo `WorkflowInstance`, `WorkflowStep`, `Admin` (`approver`).
- `WorkflowNotificationTrigger` — belongsTo `WorkflowDefinition`.
- `WorkflowTemplate` (existing, edited) — added `steps()` hasMany `WorkflowStep` and `workflowDefinitions()` hasMany `WorkflowDefinition`, now that both models exist.

Notes

- Ran `php artisan migrate` — all 7 migrations applied successfully (`workflow_definitions`, `workflow_steps`, `workflow_step_approvers`, `workflow_statuses`, `workflow_instances`, `workflow_instance_approvals`, `workflow_notification_triggers`).
- No controllers, views, routes, permissions, menu entries, `WorkflowEngineService`, `Approvable` contract, `HasWorkflow` trait, events, or listeners were created — explicitly out of scope for this step. Roadmap checklist items "Approval Levels", "Workflow Builder", "Custom Status Management" marked done (data model complete); "Single, Sequential and Parallel Approvals", "Approval History", "Rejection and Resubmission Flow", "Notification Trigger System", "Module-wise Workflow Configuration" remain unchecked pending the engine service/listener logic.
- No HRM files were touched.

### 2026-07-29 (3)

Completed

- Workflow Engine core service logic: generic engine (`Approvable` contract, `HasWorkflow` trait, `WorkflowEngineService`), events/listeners, notification bridge, and fallback-safe wiring into the 4 existing HRM approval modules (Leave Requests, Expense Claims, Attendance Adjustments, Employee Loans). No new tables, controllers, views, routes, permissions, or menu items in this step — pure backend engine + wiring, as scoped.

Database

- No new migrations. `php artisan migrate` reported "Nothing to migrate" (all 8 `workflow_*` tables from the previous step already exist).

Models

- Added `App\Contracts\Approvable` — `approvalPayload(): array`, `workflowModuleKey(): string`, mirrors `App\Contracts\GlobalSearchable`'s plain-interface style.
- Added `App\Traits\HasWorkflow` — `workflowInstance()` (`morphOne(WorkflowInstance::class, 'approvable')->latestOfMany()`) and `workflowInstances()` (`morphMany`, latest-first). Default Laravel morph-name convention (`approvable_type`/`approvable_id`) matches the actual column names on `workflow_instances` exactly, so no explicit column overrides were needed.
- `LeaveRequest`, `ExpenseClaim`, `AttendanceAdjustment`, `EmployeeLoan` now `implements Approvable` and `use HasWorkflow`; each got a small `approvalPayload()` (key display fields) and a `workflowModuleKey()` (`leave_request`, `expense_claim`, `attendance_adjustment`, `employee_loan`).

Services

- Added `App\Services\WorkflowEngineService` — fully generic, never references a concrete HRM model:
  - `start($approvable, $initiatedByAdminId)` — resolves the active `WorkflowDefinition` for `get_class($approvable)` (`approvable_type` + `status = true`), throws `RuntimeException` if none found, creates a `WorkflowInstance` at the first `workflow_steps.step_order`, `current_status = 'pending'`.
  - `act($instance, $approverAdminId, $action, $remarks)` — logs a `WorkflowInstanceApproval` row; `rejected` is reject-fast (sets `current_status = rejected`, `completed_at`, fires `WorkflowRejected` immediately); `approved` checks the current step's `approval_type` (`single`/`all_must_approve`/`any_one_approves`) against approvals already logged for that step+instance to decide whether to advance to the next `step_order`, complete (fires `WorkflowApproved`), or wait for more approvers; `on_hold`/`commented` are log-only.
  - `resubmit($approvable, $initiatedByAdminId)` — requires the latest instance for that approvable to be `current_status = 'rejected'`; creates a new instance with `resubmission_of` = old instance id and `resubmission_count` = old + 1 (both columns already existed on `workflow_instances` from the prior migration step — no schema changes needed here), logs a `resubmitted` approval row on the OLD instance, fires `WorkflowResubmitted`.
- Added `App\Services\WorkflowNotifier` — given an instance + event name, loads matching `workflow_notification_triggers` rows for that definition, resolves recipients per `notify_type` (`initiator` → `instance.initiated_by`; `approver` → current step's `workflow_step_approvers`, resolving `role`/`user`/`designation` approver types to admin IDs; `role`/`user` trigger-level → `notify_id`), writes one `ActivityLog` row per recipient via the existing `ActivityLogger` trait (`module = 'Workflow'`, `action = $event`) then one `Notification` row (`activity_log_id` set, `title`/`message` built from `template_message` with `{module}`/`{instance_id}`/`{status}`/`{event}` placeholder substitution, or a sensible default string if no template is set).
- `WorkflowEngineService` calls `WorkflowNotifier` at `start` (`step_pending`), on step advance (`step_pending` again for the new step), on final completion (`approved`), on rejection (`rejected`), and on resubmission (`resubmitted`) — these five values are exactly the `workflow_notification_triggers.event` enum members, no invented event names.

Events / Listeners

- Added `App\Events\WorkflowApproved`, `WorkflowRejected`, `WorkflowResubmitted`, `WorkflowStepAdvanced` (plain `Dispatchable`, `public readonly WorkflowInstance $instance` constructor property). `WorkflowStepAdvanced` fires on intermediate step advances only (not consumed by the HRM sync listeners; reserved for future consumers / already covered by the notifier's `step_pending` trigger).
- Added `App\Listeners\SyncLeaveRequestApproval`, `SyncExpenseClaimApproval`, `SyncAttendanceAdjustmentApproval`, `SyncEmployeeLoanApproval` — each has typed `handleApproved(WorkflowApproved)`, `handleRejected(WorkflowRejected)`, `handleResubmitted(WorkflowResubmitted)` methods (Laravel 12 auto-discovery style: no prior `EventServiceProvider`/`app/Events`/`app/Listeners` convention existed in this codebase, and `bootstrap/providers.php` only registers `AppServiceProvider`, so default Laravel 12 event-to-listener auto-discovery was used — confirmed working via `php artisan event:clear` + a route/model smoke test, no manual registration file added). Each listener guards on `$event->instance->approvable_type === <Model>::class` before acting, then calls that module's **existing** Service `approve()`/`reject()` method unchanged. On `WorkflowResubmitted`, each listener directly resets that module's own `approval_status` column back to `'pending'` via `Model::where('id', ...)->update(...)` instead of adding new service methods — chosen to keep the diff to existing HRM services at zero.

Controllers

- `LeaveRequestController`, `ExpenseClaimController`, `AttendanceAdjustmentController`, `EmployeeLoanController`: `store()` now checks `WorkflowDefinition::where('approvable_type', <Model>::class)->where('status', true)->exists()` after the existing create-and-log block, calling `WorkflowEngineService::start()` only if true (currently always false — zero `WorkflowDefinition` rows exist, so `store()` behaves identically to before). `approve()`/`reject()` wrap the single service call in an `if ($hasWorkflow) { ... } else { <exact original line> }` — the `else` branch is a byte-for-byte copy of the original call, so with no active `WorkflowDefinition` rows (today's reality) every one of these 12 methods (4 modules × store/approve/reject) executes exactly the same code path as before this task.

Notes

- **No builder UI yet**: `WorkflowDefinition` (and its `WorkflowStep`/`WorkflowStepApprover`/`WorkflowNotificationTrigger` children) can currently only be created via `php artisan tinker` or a seeder — there is no admin CRUD screen for building a workflow definition/steps/approvers/triggers. This means the Workflow Engine is fully wired end-to-end at the code level but **inert in production** until at least one `WorkflowDefinition` row is created for one of the 4 approvable types. This was explicitly out of scope for this task ("no new user-facing CRUD screens/routes/permissions/menu items").
- Verified fallback safety: ran `php artisan migrate` ("Nothing to migrate"), `php artisan event:clear`, `php artisan config:clear`, `php artisan config:cache` (succeeded — confirms no fatal PHP errors across every newly loaded class), `php -l` on all 21 new/modified files (all clean), `php artisan route:list --name=leave-requests` (all 9 routes intact, unchanged), and a tinker check confirming `LeaveRequest` now `implements Approvable` and exposes `workflowInstance()`.
- `WorkflowDefinition::scopeActive()` already existed from the prior step and is used indirectly by matching the same `where('status', true)` condition in the controllers/service, kept consistent rather than introducing a second convention.
- `App\Exceptions\NoActiveWorkflowException` was added as an available custom exception type but `WorkflowEngineService::start()`/`resubmit()` currently throw plain `RuntimeException` with a descriptive message (no prior `app/Exceptions` custom-exception convention existed in this codebase to extend) — both are acceptable per spec; kept as `RuntimeException` to match the simplest existing convention.
- Did not touch `WorkflowTemplate` model/controller/service/views/routes, per hard rule.

- Added `OpportunityRequest` — `stage` validated via `Rule::in(Opportunity::STAGES)` rather than a hardcoded array, so the Request and the model's `STAGES` constant can never drift apart.

### 2026-07-30 (5)

Completed (5 modules built sequentially in one pass, per explicit instruction to skip per-module confirmation — CRM is now 13/14 done, only CRM Dashboard and CRM Reports remain)

- Activities (Call, Meeting, Email)
- Follow Ups and Reminders
- Email Communication History

- Sales Forecasting

Database

- `activities`: `type` enum (`call`/`meeting`/`email`) default `call`, `subject` required, `description` nullable, `due_date` required datetime, `lead_id`/`contact_id`/`company_id`/`opportunity_id` all nullable FKs (`nullOnDelete`, no cross-field "at least one" requirement here — unlike Relationship History, a scheduled activity can legitimately stand alone), `assigned_to` nullable FK → `admins`, `activity_status` enum (`pending`/`completed`/`cancelled`) default `pending` — this is the real workflow-style state field (kept separate from `status`, same convention as `approval_status` on HRM's Leave Requests etc.), `status` boolean.
- `follow_ups`: `title` required, `remind_at` required datetime, `notes` nullable, same 4 nullable relation FKs as Activities, `assigned_to` nullable FK → `admins`, `is_completed` boolean default false (separate done/not-done flag, distinct from `status` which just archives the reminder record), `status` boolean.

- `quotations`: `quotation_number` unique string (auto-generated, see Services below), `lead_id`/`contact_id`/`company_id`/`opportunity_id` nullable FKs, `issue_date` required date, `valid_until` nullable date, `amount` decimal(15,2) required, `notes` nullable text, `quotation_status` enum (`draft`/`sent`/`accepted`/`rejected`/`expired`) default `draft`, `created_by` nullable FK → `admins`, `status` boolean. **Deliberately header-only, no line items** (no `quotation_items` master-detail table like `salary_structures`/`salary_structure_items`) — the roadmap's full line-item "Sales Quotations" belongs to the future Sales module; this CRM-stage Quotations feature is a lightweight single-amount quote (a total + notes summarizing what's quoted) used earlier in the pipeline, before a deal is handed off to Sales for a formal itemized quotation. This scope decision is called out explicitly here in case a future task assumes line items exist.

Models

- Added `App\Models\Quotation` — fillable incl. `quotation_number`/`quotation_status`, casts `issue_date`/`valid_until` to `date` and `amount` to `decimal:2`, `public const STATUSES`, relations `lead()`, `contact()`, `company()`, `opportunity()`, `createdBy()`.

Services

- Added `ActivityService` — standard `create()`/`update()`/`delete()` plus `updateActivityStatus()`, a small dedicated method (mirrors `OpportunityService::updateStage()`) used by the separate pending/completed/cancelled toggle endpoint so that state change doesn't require running the full `ActivityRequest` validation.

- Added `EmailCommunicationService` — standard 3 methods only.
- Added `QuotationService` — standard `update()`/`delete()`, but `create()` auto-generates `quotation_number` via a protected `generateQuotationNumber()` helper (`'QUO-' . str_pad($lastId + 1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)` off `Quotation::max('id')`) — no prior invoice/reference-numbering convention existed anywhere else in this codebase (checked: no `str_pad`/`sprintf('%06d')`/`invoice_number`/`reference_number` patterns found in `app/`), so this introduces the first one; future Sales module invoice numbering can either reuse this exact pattern or diverge — no shared helper/trait was extracted since only one module needs it today.

Requests

- Added `ActivityRequest` — `type`/`activity_status` both validated via `Rule::in()` against the model's `TYPES`/`ACTIVITY_STATUSES` constants (same "Request references the model constant, never a duplicated literal array" technique used by `OpportunityRequest` for `stage`).
- Added `FollowUpRequest` — plain field validation, `is_completed` optional boolean (only ever set via the dedicated `markCompleted()` endpoint in normal use, but accepted here too since the create/edit forms don't expose it and Laravel would otherwise strip it from `$request->validated()` on an unrelated future form field addition).
- Added `EmailCommunicationRequest` — `direction` via `Rule::in(EmailCommunication::DIRECTIONS)`; `from_email`/`to_email` validated as `email` when present.
- Added `QuotationRequest` — `quotation_status` via `Rule::in(Quotation::STATUSES)`; `valid_until` has an `after_or_equal:issue_date` cross-field rule (the only such date-ordering rule introduced in this batch — no equivalent existed to copy, but it's a standard Laravel validation rule, not custom logic). `quotation_number` is deliberately absent from the rules — it's server-generated only, never client-submitted.

Controllers

- `ActivityController` — index eager-loads all 4 relations, adds `type` and `activity_status` AJAX filters; sorts by `due_date ASC, id DESC` (soonest-due first, same chronological-sort reasoning as Relationship History's `interaction_date DESC`). - `EmailCommunicationController` — index eager-loads all 3 relations, adds a `direction` AJAX filter; `store()` injects `created_by` server-side exactly like `RelationshipHistoryController::store()`.
- `QuotationController` — index eager-loads all 4 relations, adds a `quotation_status` AJAX filter; `store()` injects `created_by` server-side; the service (not the controller) owns `quotation_number` generation, keeping the controller identical in shape to every other CRM controller.

### 2026-07-31 (2)

Completed

- Categories redesigned as a self-referencing tree (client request: "no separate Sub Category module, use `parent_id` on Categories, dynamic tree view"). This retroactively covers the roadmap's "Sub Categories" checklist item — it is intentionally **not** a separate table/module.

Database

- Added `database/migrations/2026_07_31_100000_add_parent_id_to_categories_table.php` (follow-up migration on top of the just-shipped `categories` table, not an edit to the original migration file, per standard Laravel practice): drops the old plain `unique('name')`, adds `parent_id` (nullable, `foreignId` self-referencing `categories.id`, `nullOnDelete`), adds a composite `unique(['parent_id', 'name'])`. `nullOnDelete` (not `cascadeOnDelete`) is deliberate — deleting a parent category promotes its children to top-level instead of deleting the whole subtree, verified in testing.
- Uniqueness is now scoped per-parent (same convention as `designations.unique(['department_id','name'])`) — two categories can share a name (e.g. "Phones") as long as they sit under different parents.

Models

- `App\Models\Category` — added `parent_id` to fillable; added `parent(): BelongsTo` and `children(): HasMany` (both self-referencing via `parent_id`); added `descendantIds(): array` (recursive walk of `children`, used for cycle-prevention and to exclude a node's own subtree from its "choose new parent" dropdown on edit); added `public static function indentedOptions(Collection $categories, ?int $parentId = null, int $depth = 0): array` — builds an indented `[id => label]` option list from an already-loaded flat collection (avoids N+1 queries in the create/edit views' parent dropdown).

Requests

- `App\Http\Requests\Admin\CategoryRequest` — `parent_id` nullable `exists:categories,id`, plus `Rule::notIn([$id])` on edit (a category can't be its own parent); `name` uniqueness now scoped `->where('parent_id', $this->parent_id)` instead of globally unique; added a `withValidator()` closure that calls `$category->descendantIds()` and rejects the update if the chosen `parent_id` is one of the category's own descendants (prevents creating a cycle, e.g. moving "Electronics" under its own child "Phones").

Controllers

- `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\CategoryController::index()` — no longer a Yajra DataTables AJAX endpoint. Now loads the full `Category` collection once (`orderBy('name')->get()`) and hands it to a recursive Blade partial that renders a real nested tree (acceptable query cost for an admin-only master-data screen; not paginated since category counts are expected to be small-to-moderate, same assumption `ModuleMenu` management already makes for its own parent/child tree).
- `create()` now also accepts `?parent_id=` as a query param (used by the tree's per-node "Add Subcategory" button) and passes it to the view as `$selectedParentId` to preselect that option.
- `edit()` now excludes the category itself **and** all of its descendants from the parent dropdown (`Category::orderBy('name')->get()->whereNotIn('id', $excludedIds)`), so the UI can't even present a cycle-forming option — the `CategoryRequest` cycle check is a defense-in-depth backstop, not the only guard.

Views

- Rewrote `resources/views/admin/categories/index.blade.php` — replaced the DataTables toolbar/table/footer with a real tree: search input (client-side), Expand All / Collapse All buttons, Add Category button, and a `<ul>` tree rendered via a new recursive partial `resources/views/admin/categories/_node.blade.php` (each `<li>` renders itself, then `@include`s itself again for `$children`). Each node shows an expand/collapse caret (hidden via CSS `.leaf` class when no children), name, description, the existing status switch, and 3 inline actions (Add Subcategory / Edit / Delete) — replacing the separate `action.blade.php` partial, which was deleted as dead code since nothing renders per-DataTable-row anymore.
- `create.blade.php`/`edit.blade.php` gained a "Parent Category" `.select` (Select2-enhanced) populated via `Category::indentedOptions()`.
- No JS tree-view library was added (none exists in this Bootstrap/jQuery stack) — expand/collapse and search-filter are plain jQuery show/hide against the server-rendered `<ul>`/`<li>` markup, consistent with the project's existing "no new dependency for one screen" precedent (see Opportunities Kanban's plain HTML5 drag-and-drop from the prior session).

JS

- Rewrote `public/assets/system/js/pages/categories.js` — no more DataTable init. Implements: expand/collapse per node and via Expand All/Collapse All; a client-side search filter that hides non-matching nodes and auto-expands/reveals the ancestors of any match; and `_statusUpdate()` for the existing status-switch convention. **Key reuse trick**: the shared `.ajax-form` submit handler and `#delete_item` click handler in `main.js` both call `dataTableInstance.ajax.reload(null, false)` on success and are otherwise untouched/generic across every module. Since Categories has no real DataTable anymore, `categories.js` declares a fake global `dataTableInstance = { ajax: { reload: function () { window.location.reload(); } } }` — this makes the existing shared handlers "just work" (full page reload re-renders the tree with fresh data after create/update/delete) with **zero changes to `main.js`** and no special-casing needed there for tree-based pages.

Routes / Permissions / Menu

- No changes — same 7 `categories.*` routes, same `category.view/create/edit/delete` permissions, same single "Categories" menu entry under "Product Masters". The FK/tree redesign is entirely inside the existing Category CRUD surface, not a new module.

Notes

- Ran `php artisan migrate` — the new `add_parent_id_to_categories_table` migration applied cleanly (table was empty at the time, so no data migration/backfill was needed).
- Verified end-to-end via tinker: built a real 3-level tree (Electronics → Phones → Smartphones), confirmed `descendantIds()` correctly returns grandchildren; confirmed two categories named "Phones" can coexist under different parents (per-parent uniqueness working); confirmed deleting a parent (`ParentCat` → `ChildCat`) sets the child's `parent_id` to `null` rather than deleting it (`nullOnDelete` verified, not cascade); rendered `index()`, `create()`, and `edit()` directly and called `->render()` on each — all three produced full HTML with no fatal Blade errors (93,832 / 2,566 / 2,501 chars). All test categories deleted afterward, table back to 0 rows.
- `php -l` clean on all 3 modified PHP files; `php artisan route:list --name=categories` confirmed all 7 routes unchanged; `config:clear && config:cache` succeeded.
- This changes the answer to the roadmap's "Sub Categories" checklist item from "a separate table/module" (as originally planned in the 2026-07-31 entry above) to "merged into Categories via `parent_id`" — a deliberate architecture change made at the client's explicit request, not a bug fix. Any future module needing to reference "a product category" should treat `categories` as the single source of truth regardless of its depth in the tree.
- No HRM, Workflow Engine, or CRM files were touched.

### 2026-07-31 (9)

Completed

- Product Variants (eighth and final "before Products" Product Management module — closes the ordering gap flagged in the 2026-07-31 (8) entry; combines a `Product` with one or more `AttributeValue`s into a concrete sellable SKU, e.g. "T-Shirt — Red / Large")

Database

- Added two tables in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_07_31_170000_create_product_variants_table.php`): `product_variants` (`product_id` required `foreignId` → `products.id` `cascadeOnDelete` — a variant cannot outlive its product, same reasoning as `attribute_values` → `product_attributes`; `sku` unique required; `price` nullable decimal(15,2) — a per-variant price override, falls back to the product's `selling_price` when null; `status` boolean) and `product_variant_attribute_values` (pure many-to-many pivot: `product_variant_id`/`attribute_value_id`, both `cascadeOnDelete`, named unique index `pv_av_unique` on the pair — Laravel's default auto-generated index name would have exceeded MySQL's identifier length limit given the two long table/column names, so an explicit short name was passed as the second argument to `$table->unique()`). This is the **first** true many-to-many pivot table in the Product Management module — every prior module here used simple `belongsTo` FKs.

Models

- Added `App\Models\ProductVariant` — fillable `product_id, sku, price, status`, casts `status` boolean and `price` to `decimal:2`, relations `product(): BelongsTo` and `attributeValues(): BelongsToMany` (via the `product_variant_attribute_values` pivot table, no extra pivot columns needed so no `withPivot()`/`withTimestamps()` was added), `scopeActive()`.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\ProductVariantRequest` — `product_id` required `exists:products,id`; `sku` required unique (ignoring current id via route param `product_variant`); `attribute_value_ids` required array `min:1` with each element `exists:attribute_values,id`; `price`/`status` as usual. Added a `withValidator()` closure that is new to this module: since a "duplicate variant" isn't a single-column uniqueness problem (it's "does any other variant of this same product already have this exact *set* of attribute values"), the closure loads every other variant for the submitted `product_id`, sorts each one's `attributeValues` id list, and compares it to the sorted submitted `attribute_value_ids` — flagging a validation error if any match. A DB-level unique constraint can't express "same set of pivot rows", so this app-level check is the only guard (documented here since it's a new pattern for this codebase, not copied from an existing module).

Services

- Added `App\Services\ProductVariantService` — `create()`/`update()` both pull `attribute_value_ids` out of the validated array before calling `ProductVariant::create()`/`update()` (since it isn't a real column), then call `$variant->attributeValues()->sync($attributeValueIds)` to write the pivot rows. `delete()` is a plain model delete — the pivot rows cascade via the FK, not via Eloquent pivot-detach logic, so no extra code was needed there (verified in testing).

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\ProductVariantController` — index eager-loads `product` and `attributeValues`, adds a `product_id` AJAX filter, search matches the variant `sku` or its product's `name`. The single `variant` display column renders "<Product Name> — <value 1> / <value 2>" (e.g. "T-Shirt — Red / Large") from the loaded `attributeValues` pluck. `create()`/`edit()` load all active `AttributeValue`s **grouped by their parent attribute's name** (`->groupBy(fn($av) => $av->productAttribute->name ?? 'Other')`) so the form can render one checkbox row per attribute (Color: Red/Blue/Green, Size: Small/Large) instead of one flat unlabeled list. `edit()` additionally computes `$selectedAttributeValueIds` via `$productVariant->attributeValues()->pluck('attribute_values.id')` (explicit table-qualified column, required since both sides of the pivot join have an `id` column) to pre-check the right boxes.

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/product-variants/{index,create,edit,action}.blade.php` — `index.blade.php` adds an "All Products" filter dropdown (same placement as every other relation-filtered index in this project). `create.blade.php`/`edit.blade.php` render the grouped attribute-value checkboxes via `@forelse($attributeValues as $attributeName => $values)` with a small muted group label per attribute, plus a "Price Override" field explicitly labelled as falling back to the product's price when left empty. This is the first Product Management form using checkboxes instead of a `.select`/Select2 dropdown, since a variant is defined by potentially *multiple* simultaneous attribute values (Color AND Size), not a single FK pick.
- Added `public/assets/system/js/pages/product-variants.js` — standard DataTable init pattern plus the `product_id` filter value, same technique used throughout.

Routes

- Added `routes/admin.php` block `// Product Management - Product Variants` (status POST + `Route::resource('product-variants', ...)->except(['show'])`), placed directly after the Products block, inside the existing `isAdmin` middleware group. Route-model-binding param is `{product_variant}`.

Permissions

- Added `product-variant.view/create/edit/delete` to `database/seeders/RolePermissionSeeder.php` under the existing "Product Management" comment block, directly after `product.*`. Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker per established precedent.

Menu

- **Known limitation, documented rather than silently left in place**: deleting a `Product` cascades at the database FK level, which removes `product_images` rows directly — it does **not** run through `ProductImageService::delete()`, so the physical image files on the `public` disk are **not** automatically cleaned up when a product (and therefore its images) is deleted this way (confirmed in the same tinker test: both uploaded files remained on disk after the cascade-deleted rows disappeared, and had to be removed manually). This is a pre-existing class of gap in this codebase's cascade-delete + file-storage combination (the same risk exists anywhere a `cascadeOnDelete` FK points at a table with a stored file path, e.g. potentially `employee_documents` if an `employees` row were ever hard-deleted) — fixing it properly (a model `deleting` event listener on `Product` that walks its images and deletes files first) was judged out of scope for a single new module and would need to be applied consistently across every file-owning table, not just this one; flagging it here for whoever picks up file-storage cleanup as a cross-cutting concern later.

This is the **first true master-detail (header + line items) pattern in Product Management** — mirrors the existing `SalaryStructure`/`SalaryStructureItem` and `WorkflowDefinition`/`WorkflowStep` precedents from HRM/Workflow Engine, not a new pattern for this codebase overall.

Models

- Added `App\Models\ProductBundle` — fillable `sku, name, description, price, status`, casts `status` boolean and `price` to `decimal:2`, relation `items(): HasMany` (→ `ProductBundleItem`), `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\ProductBundleItem` — fillable `product_bundle_id, product_id, quantity`, relations `productBundle()`/`product()` (both `belongsTo`).

Services

- Added `App\Services\ProductBundleService` — follows the exact `SalaryStructureService` "delete-then-recreate" master-detail sync convention: `create()`/`update()` pull `items` out of the validated array, write the header row, then `syncItems()` deletes all existing `ProductBundleItem` rows for that bundle and recreates them fresh from the submitted array (simpler and safer than diffing old vs. new rows, same tradeoff `SalaryStructureService::syncItems()` already accepted). `delete()` is a plain model delete (items cascade via FK).

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\ProductBundleRequest` — `sku` required unique (ignoring current id via route param `product_bundle`); `name` required; `price` nullable numeric `min:0`; `items` required array `min:1` (a bundle needs at least one product); `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` (blocks adding the same product twice in one bundle — `distinct` is Laravel's built-in rule for this, no custom closure needed) `exists:products,id`; `items.*.quantity` required integer `min:1`.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\ProductBundleController` — index uses `withCount('items')` (not `with('items')`) since the DataTable only needs the item count, not the full item list, avoiding an unnecessary N+1-prevention eager load of data never displayed. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger` so the activity log captures the full bundle+items snapshot, same technique `WorkflowDefinitionController` uses (`->load('steps.approvers')`) for its nested tree.

- Added `public/assets/system/js/pages/product-bundles.js` — `buildBundleItemRow()` clones the hidden product-options `<select>`'s HTML into each new row (so every row gets its own independent Select2-ready dropdown) plus a quantity input and a remove button; `populateExistingBundleItems()` + a `MutationObserver` on `#modal_remote .modal-content` reads the `data-existing` JSON and rebuilds one row per existing item when the edit modal is injected — this is a verbatim adaptation of `workflow-definitions.js`'s `buildWorkflowStepRow`/`populateExistingWorkflowSteps`/`observeModalContent` trio, renamed for bundles.

- Added `routes/admin.php` block `// Product Management - Product Bundles` (status POST + `Route::resource('product-bundles', ...)->except(['show'])`), placed directly after the Product Images block, inside the existing `isAdmin` middleware group. Route-model-binding param is `{product_bundle}`.

Notes

- Ran `php artisan migrate` — `2026_07_31_190000_create_product_bundles_table` applied successfully, creating both `product_bundles` and `product_bundle_items` with all FK constraints (`products`) intact.
- Verified end-to-end: `php -l` on all 8 new/modified PHP files (all clean), `php artisan route:list --name=product-bundles` shows all 7 routes with correct route-model-binding param name `product_bundle`, `php artisan config:clear && config:cache` succeeded, permissions confirmed synced to Super Admin (4 rows). Ran a full tinker lifecycle test: created two real `Product` rows, created a `ProductBundle` with both as items (qty 2 and qty 1) via `ProductBundleService::create()`, confirmed both items loaded correctly with the right quantities; called `update()` with a completely different single-item list and confirmed the old two items were fully replaced (delete-then-recreate sync working as intended, not merged/diffed); then deleted one of the two component **products** directly (not the bundle) and confirmed its `ProductBundleItem` row cascade-deleted while the bundle header row itself survived untouched.
- **Data-integrity note, documented rather than silently accepted**: because `product_bundle_items.product_id` is `cascadeOnDelete`, deleting a component `Product` silently removes it from every bundle that referenced it — if that was a bundle's *only* item, the bundle is left with zero items even though `ProductBundleRequest` requires `min:1` at create/update time. The `min:1` rule is therefore only enforced going forward (on the next edit), not as an ongoing DB-level guarantee. This is the same category of gap as the Product Images orphaned-file note in the previous entry (a `cascadeOnDelete` FK reaching into another table's business-rule invariant) but was judged lower severity (a data-quality inconsistency, not an accumulating resource leak) and left as-is rather than spawning a second cross-cutting follow-up task for it.

No Model, no Service, no Form Request in the usual CRUD sense (mirrors the `HrReportController`/`SalesForecastController`/`CrmDashboardController` precedent of a pure-read feature needing none of those layers), except this one does have simple request validation on the print step since it accepts user-submitted `product_ids[]`/`quantity[]` arrays.

Dependency decision

- **No Composer package was added.** Checked `composer.json` first — no barcode library (`picqer/php-barcode-generator`, `milon/barcode`, etc.) was already installed. Rather than adding a new backend dependency for one feature, barcodes are rendered **client-side** via the `JsBarcode` JS library loaded from a CDN (`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jsbarcode@3.11.6/...`) — same "avoid a new dependency for one feature" precedent already set by CSV import/export using plain PHP `fputcsv`/`fgetcsv` instead of `maatwebsite/excel`, and by Chart.js/FullCalendar already being loaded via CDN elsewhere in this project rather than as Composer/npm packages.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\BarcodeGeneratorController` — `index()` lists all active products for selection (no DataTable; a plain table with a client-side JS text-filter, since the interaction is "check boxes and set quantities," not paginate/sort/search a large dataset the DataTables way). `print(Request $request)` validates `product_ids` (required array, each `exists:products,id`) and an optional `quantity` array (`nullable|integer|min:1|max:100` per product, defaulting to 1), expands the selection into a flat `$labels` array with one entry per copy (a product requesting 3 copies appears 3 times in `$labels`), and returns a **separate standalone print view** (not wrapped in `admin.layout.app` — no sidebar/topbar chrome, since this is meant to open in a new tab and go straight to the printer).

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/barcode-generator/index.blade.php` — extends the normal admin layout; a plain `<table>` (not DataTables — this doesn't need server-side pagination for a "select some products" screen) with one checkbox + quantity input per active product, a client-side JS name-filter (`indexOf` against a lowercased `data-name` attribute, same lightweight technique the Categories tree page's search box uses), "Select All"/"Clear All" buttons, and a form `target="_blank"` GET-submitting straight to the print route so the label sheet opens in a new tab.
- Added `resources/views/admin/barcode-generator/print.blade.php` — a **complete standalone HTML document** (`<!doctype html>`...`</html>`, not a Blade `@extends` of the admin layout) since it's a print target, not an admin screen — loads `JsBarcode` via the CDN script tag, renders one `.label` `<div>` per entry in `$labels` (product name, an empty `<svg class="barcode" data-code="{{ $product->sku }}">`, and the selling price if set), then a small inline `<script>` block that calls `JsBarcode(el, el.dataset.code, {format: 'CODE128', ...})` on every `.barcode` element once the page loads. `@media print { .print-actions { display: none } .label { border: none } }` hides the on-screen "Print" button and removes the dashed label borders when actually printing.

Routes

- Added `routes/admin.php` block `// Product Management - Barcode Generator`: `GET barcode-generator` (`admin.barcode-generator.index`) and `GET barcode-generator/print` (`admin.barcode-generator.print`) — both plain `GET` routes, no `Route::resource`, matching the `hr-reports`/`sales-forecast` shape (a feature with no create/edit/delete concept doesn't get resource routes). `print` is `GET` (not `POST`) specifically so the index form's `target="_blank"` submission opens a normal browser tab the user can print/close, rather than requiring a same-tab POST redirect dance.

### 2026-08-01 (6)

Completed

- Sales Quotations (sixth Sales module — the fuller, master-detail Sales-stage quotation, distinct from the lightweight single-amount CRM Quotations built earlier)

Scope decision (inspected before building, per task instruction)

- Inspected the existing CRM `QuotationController`/`QuotationService`/`Quotation` model first. CRM's `quotations` table is a **flat, header-only** entity (single manual `amount` field, no line items, FKs to `lead_id`/`contact_id`/`company_id`/`opportunity_id`) — appropriate for an early-pipeline lightweight quote before a deal reaches Sales. It could not be reused or extended for this task: it has no `customer_id` FK (Sales' `customers` table didn't exist yet when CRM Quotations was built), no product line items, and retrofitting either onto it would blur two conceptually different documents (a rough CRM-stage estimate vs. a real itemized Sales quotation feeding future Sales Orders/Invoices).
- Instead, reused the **Product Bundles / Price Lists master-detail pattern** (header + `hasMany` items, delete-then-recreate sync service) since it already models exactly this shape (SKU-style header, repeatable product line items). Reused CRM `QuotationService::generateQuotationNumber()`'s numbering technique (`str_pad(max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`) but with prefix `SQ-` instead of `QUO-`, scoped to the new `SalesQuotation` model's own `id` sequence, to avoid any confusion between the two document types' reference numbers.
- **Naming collision avoided per the Naming/Table Conflict Guard convention**: the new tables are `sales_quotations` / `sales_quotation_items`, NOT `quotations` (already owned by CRM). Models are `SalesQuotation`/`SalesQuotationItem`, routes/permissions/menu all prefixed `sales-quotation(s)`, so there is zero overlap with the CRM `Quotation` model, `quotations.*` routes, or `quotation.*` permissions.

Database

- Added `sales_quotations`/`sales_quotation_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_140000_create_sales_quotations_table.php`), mirroring the `price_lists`/`price_list_items` two-tables-in-one-migration precedent:
  - `sales_quotations`: `quotation_number` unique (server-generated); `customer_id` required `foreignId` → `customers.id`, **`cascadeOnDelete`** (a quotation is meaningless without its customer, same "required parent-owns-child FK" reasoning as `product_bundle_items`/`price_list_items` → `products` — verified in testing that deleting the customer cascades away its quotations, not `nullOnDelete`, since an orphaned quotation with no customer would be nonsensical); `payment_term_id` nullable `foreignId` → `payment_terms.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `issue_date` required date, `valid_until` nullable date (`after_or_equal:issue_date` at the Form Request level, same rule already used by `Quotation.valid_until`/`DiscountRule.end_date`); `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` decimal(15,2) default 0 — all three are **server-computed from line items**, never client-submitted (stripped from the Form Request's rules, computed in the Service); `quotation_status` enum (`draft`/`sent`/`accepted`/`rejected`/`expired`) default `draft` — same 5-value enum CRM's `Quotation::STATUSES` already established, reused verbatim as `SalesQuotation::STATUSES` since it's the same conceptual lifecycle, just a different table; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `sales_quotation_items`: `sales_quotation_id`/`product_id`, both `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as bundles/price-list items); `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1 (decimal, not integer — allows fractional quantities e.g. 2.5 kg, unlike `ProductBundleItem.quantity` which is a plain integer since bundle composition is always whole units); `unit_price` decimal(15,2) required; `discount` decimal(15,2) default 0 (a flat per-line discount amount, not a percentage — kept simple for this first Sales Quotations pass, matching the "no over-engineering" project rule; a percentage-based option can be added later if a real client request calls for it); `line_total` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed as `(quantity * unit_price) - discount`. **Deliberately no unique constraint** on `(sales_quotation_id, product_id)` — unlike `price_list_items`/`product_bundle_items`, the same product can legitimately appear on multiple lines of one quotation (e.g. two different discount rates for the same item), so `items.*.product_id` is validated `distinct` at the Form Request level only as a UX safeguard against accidental duplicate rows, not enforced at the DB level.

Models

- Added `App\Models\SalesQuotation` — fillable `quotation_number, customer_id, payment_term_id, issue_date, valid_until, subtotal, discount_total, grand_total, quotation_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES` (mirrors `Quotation::STATUSES` exactly); casts `status` boolean, `issue_date`/`valid_until` to `date`, the three total fields to `decimal:2`; relations `customer()`, `paymentTerm()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `SalesQuotationItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\SalesQuotationItem` — fillable `sales_quotation_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, discount, line_total`; casts all four numeric fields to `decimal:2`; relations `salesQuotation()`, `product()`.

Services

- Added `App\Services\SalesQuotationService` — follows the `PriceListService`/`ProductBundleService` delete-then-recreate `syncItems()` convention, extended with genuinely new logic for this module:
  - `generateQuotationNumber()` — `'SQ-' . str_pad(SalesQuotation::max('id') + 1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, called automatically inside `create()` (never client-submitted, same as `Quotation.quotation_number`/`Customer.customer_code`).
  - `calculateTotals(array $items)` — new method, not present in any prior master-detail service in this codebase (Product Bundles/Price Lists have no header-level money totals to roll up): sums `quantity * unit_price` across all submitted items into `subtotal`, sums each line's `discount` into `discount_total`, and computes `grand_total = subtotal - discount_total`. Called by both `create()` and `update()` before writing the header row, so `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` are always derived fresh from whatever the current `items` payload is — there is no drift risk between the header totals and the line items, since both are written in the same request from the same source array.
  - `syncItems()` — same delete-then-recreate strategy as `PriceListService`, additionally computing each line's `line_total = (quantity * unit_price) - discount` before creating the `SalesQuotationItem` row (so `line_total` is always stored pre-computed, not calculated on the fly at display time).

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\SalesQuotationRequest` — `customer_id` required `exists:customers,id`; `payment_term_id` nullable `exists:payment_terms,id`; `issue_date` required date; `valid_until` nullable `after_or_equal:issue_date`; `quotation_status` required `Rule::in(SalesQuotation::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1`; `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id`; `items.*.quantity` required numeric `min:0.01` (not integer, matching the decimal `quantity` column); `items.*.unit_price` required numeric `min:0`; `items.*.discount` nullable numeric `min:0`. `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total`/`quotation_number` are all deliberately absent from the rules — server-computed/generated only.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\SalesQuotationController` — index eager-loads `customer`/`paymentTerm` and `withCount('items')`; adds `customer_id`/`quotation_status` AJAX filters beyond the standard `status`/`search`; search matches `quotation_number` or (via `orWhereHas`) the customer's `name`. DataTable columns: `quotation_number` (with customer name subtitle, same "name + small subtitle" idiom used throughout this project), `items_count_label`, `issue_date_formatted`, `grand_total_formatted`, `quotation_status_badge` (color-coded per status, same idiom as CRM's `Opportunity`/`Quotation` status badges), `status_badge`. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as Product Bundles/Price Lists/Workflow Definitions.

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/sales-quotations/{index,create,edit,action}.blade.php`. `index.blade.php` uses `'modal' => 'xl'` (not the `'lg'` every prior master-detail module in this project used) — a deliberate, documented deviation: a quotation line row has 4 inputs (product/qty/price/discount) plus a remove button versus bundles'/price-lists' 2, so the wider modal was chosen for readability; there is no established `'xl'` convention being violated since none previously existed for this shape of form (confirmed neither `product-bundles` nor `price-lists` uses `'xl'`). Adds "All Customers" and "All Quotation Status" filter dropdowns in the toolbar (same placement/style as every other relation/enum filter in this project).
- `create.blade.php`/`edit.blade.php` are adaptations of the `price-lists` repeatable-row builder: header fields (Customer, Payment Term, Issue Date, Valid Until, Quotation Status, Status, Notes) in the usual `fm-grid`, then a `.sales-quotation-item-rows` container + "Add Item" button, a hidden `<select class="d-none sales-quotation-product-options">` product-options source (each `<option>` carries a `data-price` attribute set to the product's `selling_price`, a new addition beyond what bundles/price-lists' hidden select carries — used for the unit-price auto-fill described below), and (edit only) a `data-existing` JSON attribute seeding `[{product_id, quantity, unit_price, discount}, ...]` for the JS to hydrate on modal open. Both forms also render a small live totals summary block (`.sq-subtotal-preview`/`.sq-discount-preview`/`.sq-grandtotal-preview`) — a new UI element not present in Product Bundles/Price Lists, since those have no money totals to preview; the real totals are always recomputed server-side by `SalesQuotationService::calculateTotals()` regardless of what this preview shows, so it's purely a UX convenience with no trust placed in client-submitted totals.

JS

- Added `public/assets/system/js/pages/sales-quotations.js` — the `buildSalesQuotationItemRow`/`populateExistingSalesQuotationItems`/`observeModalContent` trio is a direct adaptation of `price-lists.js`'s equivalent functions, extended with a `quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount` triple per row instead of a single `price` field. New logic beyond the bundles/price-lists precedent: (1) a `change` handler on `.sq-item-product` that auto-fills the row's `unit_price` field from the selected product's `data-price` attribute, only when the price field is currently empty (never overwrites a value the admin already typed/edited); (2) `recalculateSalesQuotationTotals(container)`, run on every item add/remove and on every `input` event on the quantity/price/discount fields, which walks all current rows and updates the three `.sq-*-preview` elements client-side in real time — this is a new client-side computation pattern not present in any prior master-detail module's JS in this codebase (Bundles/Price Lists have no money totals to preview), included purely for admin UX; the authoritative totals are always the ones `SalesQuotationService::calculateTotals()` computes server-side on submit.

Routes

- Added `routes/admin.php` block `// Sales - Sales Quotations` (status POST + `Route::resource('sales-quotations', ...)->except(['show'])`), placed directly after the Price Lists block, inside the existing `isAdmin` middleware group. Route-model-binding param is `{sales_quotation}`. Added `use App\Http\Controllers\Admin\SalesQuotationController;` alongside the other Sales controller imports.

Permissions

- Added `sales-quotation.view/create/edit/delete` to `database/seeders/RolePermissionSeeder.php` under the existing "Sales" comment block, directly after `price-list.*`. Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker per established precedent (seeder still not idempotent, not re-run wholesale).

Menu

- Extended `database/seeders/SalesMenuSeeder.php` (existing file, not duplicated) with a new **top-level direct link** "Quotations" → `admin.sales-quotations.index` at `order = 1` (right below the existing "Customers" top-level link at `order = 0`) — a quotation is a primary transactional entity, same reasoning as Customers/Products/Leads/Employees each getting their own top-level link rather than sitting inside a "Masters" group. The "Sales Masters" group's `order` was bumped from `1` to `2` to keep sibling `order` values unique among the module's `parent_id = null` rows, same order-collision-avoidance fix already applied for Product Management's Products/Product Variants/Product Bundles top-level links. Re-ran `php artisan db:seed --class=SalesMenuSeeder` — safe, `updateOrCreate` throughout; confirmed the existing "Customers" row and the "Sales Masters" group + its 3 children (Customer Groups/Payment Terms/Price Lists) were untouched, with a new top-level "Quotations" row added.

Notes

- Ran `php artisan migrate` — `2026_08_01_140000_create_sales_quotations_table` applied successfully, creating both `sales_quotations` and `sales_quotation_items` with all FK constraints (`customers`, `payment_terms`, `products`) intact.
- Verified end-to-end: `php -l` on all 9 new/modified PHP files (all clean), `php artisan route:list --name=sales-quotations` shows all 7 routes with correct route-model-binding param name `sales_quotation`, `php artisan config:clear && config:cache` succeeded, permissions confirmed synced to Super Admin (4 rows). ### 2026-08-01 (7)

Completed

- Sales Orders (seventh Sales module — a customer order, same header+line-items master-detail shape as Sales Quotations, optionally originating from one)

Database

- Added `sales_orders`/`sales_order_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_150000_create_sales_orders_table.php`), mirroring the `sales_quotations`/`sales_quotation_items` shape almost exactly:
  - `sales_orders`: `order_number` unique (server-generated); `customer_id` required `foreignId` → `customers.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as `sales_quotations.customer_id` — an order is meaningless without its customer, verified in testing); `sales_quotation_id` **nullable** `foreignId` → `sales_quotations.id`, **`nullOnDelete`** (deliberately different from `customer_id`'s cascade — an order that originated from a quotation is still a valid, independent business record once created; if the source quotation is later deleted, the order should survive with just its `sales_quotation_id` cleared, not be deleted itself, verified in testing); `payment_term_id` nullable, `nullOnDelete` (same as Sales Quotations); `order_date` required date, `expected_delivery_date` nullable date (`after_or_equal:order_date`); `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only (same convention as Sales Quotations); `order_status` enum (`pending`/`confirmed`/`processing`/`completed`/`cancelled`) default `pending` — a **different 5-value enum from `SalesQuotation::STATUSES`**, since an order's lifecycle (fulfillment-oriented) is conceptually distinct from a quotation's (approval-oriented: draft/sent/accepted/rejected/expired) — not reused, a new `SalesOrder::STATUSES` constant; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `sales_order_items`: identical shape to `sales_quotation_items` (`sales_order_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`, `quantity` decimal default 1, `unit_price` decimal required, `discount` decimal default 0 flat amount, `line_total` decimal default 0 server-computed). No unique constraint on `(sales_order_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as Sales Quotations — the same product can appear on multiple order lines.

Models

- Added `App\Models\SalesOrder` — fillable `order_number, customer_id, sales_quotation_id, payment_term_id, order_date, expected_delivery_date, subtotal, discount_total, grand_total, order_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['pending','confirmed','processing','completed','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `order_date`/`expected_delivery_date` to `date`, the three totals to `decimal:2`; relations `customer()`, `salesQuotation()`, `paymentTerm()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `SalesOrderItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\SalesOrderItem` — fillable `sales_order_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, discount, line_total`; casts all four numeric fields to `decimal:2`; relations `salesOrder()`, `product()`.
- **No new relation was added on `SalesQuotation`** (e.g. `salesOrders(): HasMany`) — not needed by anything built in this task (no UI currently lists "orders derived from this quotation"); can be added trivially later if a future feature needs it, avoiding speculative relations per the project's no-over-engineering rule.

Services

- Added `App\Services\SalesOrderService` — file-for-file structural copy of `SalesQuotationService`: `generateOrderNumber()` (`'SO-' . str_pad(SalesOrder::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)` — a new `SO-` prefix, distinct from Sales Quotations' `SQ-` and CRM's `QUO-`, so all three document types' reference numbers are visually unambiguous), `calculateTotals()` (identical subtotal/discount_total/grand_total roll-up logic), and `syncItems()` (identical delete-then-recreate strategy with per-line `line_total` computation). Requests

### 2026-08-01 (8)

Completed

- Delivery Management (eighth Sales module — a shipment/logistics record against a Sales Order, distinct from the future "Delivery Notes" printable document)

Scope decision

- A delivery tracks **what was actually shipped** for a given sales order (carrier, tracking number, delivery status, and the products/quantities shipped) — a logistics record, not a financial document, so unlike Sales Quotations/Orders it has **no pricing fields** (`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total`/`subtotal`/`grand_total`) on its line items, just `product_id` + `quantity`.
- **Key design decision, documented since it deviates from the otherwise-identical master-detail pattern**: `delivery_items` references `product_id` only, **not** a hard FK to a specific `sales_order_items` row. Reason: `SalesOrderService::syncItems()` (built in the previous task) deletes and recreates every `SalesOrderItem` row on **every** order update — a delivery FK'd to a specific `sales_order_item.id` would silently break (via `nullOnDelete`/`cascadeOnDelete` firing) the next time that order's items were edited, even if the product itself was untouched. This is the same class of "cascade FK reaching into another table's business invariant" risk already flagged twice before in this project (Product Images' orphaned files, Product Bundles' cascade-emptied bundles) — here it was avoided upfront by design rather than accepted and documented after the fact: a delivery only needs to know **which sales order** and **which products/quantities** were shipped, not a specific transient order-line row.

Database

- Added `deliveries`/`delivery_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_160000_create_deliveries_table.php`):
  - `deliveries`: `delivery_number` unique (server-generated); `sales_order_id` required `foreignId` → `sales_orders.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (a delivery record is meaningless without its order, same reasoning as `sales_orders.customer_id`); `delivery_date` required date; `carrier` nullable string; `tracking_number` nullable string; `delivery_status` enum (`pending`/`in_transit`/`delivered`/`cancelled`) default `pending` — a **third, distinct** status enum in the Sales module (different from both `SalesQuotation::STATUSES` and `SalesOrder::STATUSES`), reflecting a genuinely different lifecycle (physical shipment, not approval or fulfillment-processing); `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `delivery_items`: `delivery_id` `cascadeOnDelete`, `product_id` `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as every prior line-item table), `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1 — no price/discount/line_total columns, per the scope decision above. No unique constraint on `(delivery_id, product_id)` — same reasoning as Sales Quotations/Orders (a product could conceivably need two lines, e.g. different batch/serial tracking added in a future module).

Models

- Added `App\Models\Delivery` — fillable `delivery_number, sales_order_id, delivery_date, carrier, tracking_number, delivery_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['pending','in_transit','delivered','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `delivery_date` to `date`; relations `salesOrder()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `DeliveryItem`); `scopeActive()`. **No direct `customer()` relation** — the customer is reached via `$delivery->salesOrder->customer`, avoiding a redundant denormalized `customer_id` column that would need to always agree with the order's own customer.
- Added `App\Models\DeliveryItem` — fillable `delivery_id, product_id, quantity`; casts `quantity` to `decimal:2`; relations `delivery()`, `product()`.
- **No new relation was added on `SalesOrder`** (e.g. `deliveries(): HasMany`) — not needed by anything built in this task, same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning as the `SalesQuotation`→`SalesOrder` non-relation noted in the previous entry; trivial to add later if a future "delivery history per order" view needs it.

Services

- Added `App\Services\DeliveryService` — same delete-then-recreate `syncItems()` shape as every prior master-detail service, simplified (no totals to compute, since there's no pricing on this document): `generateDeliveryNumber()` — `'DLV-' . str_pad(Delivery::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, a number prefix distinct from `SQ-`/`SO-`/`QUO-`, deliberately reserving `DN-` as the likely prefix for the upcoming "Delivery Notes" module so the two don't collide once that's built.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\DeliveryRequest` — `sales_order_id` required `exists:sales_orders,id`; `delivery_date` required date; `carrier`/`tracking_number` nullable strings; `delivery_status` required `Rule::in(Delivery::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1`; `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id`; `items.*.quantity` required numeric `min:0.01`. No price/discount rules, matching the schema.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\DeliveryController` — index eager-loads `salesOrder.customer` (nested eager-load, needed since Delivery has no direct customer relation) and `withCount('items')`; adds `sales_order_id`/`delivery_status` AJAX filters; search matches `delivery_number`, `tracking_number`, or (via `orWhereHas`) the linked order's `order_number`. DataTable's `delivery_number` column subtitles both the order number and customer name (`$row->salesOrder->order_number . ' · ' . $row->salesOrder->customer->name`) so an admin can identify the delivery's context without opening it. `delivery_status_badge` has its own color map (`in_transit` → info, `delivered` → success, `cancelled` → danger) and converts the `in_transit` enum value's underscore to a space for display (`ucfirst(str_replace('_', ' ', ...))`) — a small new formatting detail not needed by the single-word statuses in Sales Quotations/Orders. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as every prior master-detail module.

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/deliveries/{index,create,edit,action}.blade.php` — uses `'modal' => 'lg'` (not `'xl'` like Sales Quotations/Orders), since each item row here only has 2 inputs (product + quantity, no price/discount), matching Product Bundles'/Price Lists' original `'lg'` sizing precedent for that simpler row shape. `index.blade.php` adds "All Orders" and "All Delivery Status" filter dropdowns. `create.blade.php`/`edit.blade.php`: header fields (Sales Order, Delivery Date, Carrier, Tracking Number, Delivery Status, Status, Notes) plus the repeatable `.delivery-item-rows` builder (product + quantity only, no live totals preview since there's nothing to total).

JS

No totals-preview logic, since this document has no pricing.

Routes

Route-model-binding param is `{delivery}`. Added `use App\Http\Controllers\Admin\DeliveryController;` alongside the other Sales controller imports.

Permissions

- Added `delivery.view/create/edit/delete` to `database/seeders/RolePermissionSeeder.php` under the existing "Sales" comment block, directly after `sales-order.*`. Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker per established precedent.

The "Sales Masters" group's `order` was bumped from `3` to `4` to keep sibling `order` values unique.
