### 2026-08-01 (9)

Completed

- Delivery Notes (ninth Sales module — the formal printable document issued for a Delivery, distinct from Delivery Management's logistics tracking record)

Scope decision

- A Delivery already tracks **what was shipped** (carrier, tracking number, delivery status, product/quantity lines). A Delivery Note is the **formal document** handed to/signed by the recipient confirming receipt — a different concern (proof-of-delivery paperwork vs. shipment tracking), so it's a separate module per the roadmap checklist rather than folding new fields onto `deliveries`.
- **Deliberately no duplicate items table.** A `DeliveryNote` is modeled as a thin **one-to-one header record** on top of an existing `Delivery` (`delivery_id` unique FK) — `note_number`, `issued_date`, `received_by`, `received_date`, `remarks`, `status`. The document's line items are read straight from `$deliveryNote->delivery->items` at print/display time rather than being copied into a new `delivery_note_items` table — avoiding the same "two tables that must always agree" duplication risk already flagged for Product Bundles/Price Lists/Sales Quotations/Orders elsewhere in this project, and there's no product/qty/price data unique to the note itself that would justify a second items table.
- Added `Delivery::deliveryNote(): HasOne` (the inverse of `DeliveryNote::delivery()`) since the controller genuinely needs it (to exclude deliveries that already have a note from the create dropdown) — not a speculative relation.

Database

- Added `delivery_notes` (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_170000_create_delivery_notes_table.php`): `note_number` unique (server-generated); `delivery_id` required `foreignId` → `deliveries.id`, **`unique()`** (enforces the one-note-per-delivery rule at the DB level, not just the app level) **and** `cascadeOnDelete` (a delivery note is meaningless without its delivery — verified in testing that deleting the delivery removes its note); `issued_date` required date; `received_by` nullable string; `received_date` nullable date (`after_or_equal:issued_date` at the Form Request level); `remarks` nullable text; `status` boolean. No line-items table, per the scope decision above.

Models

- Added `App\Models\DeliveryNote` — fillable `note_number, delivery_id, issued_date, received_by, received_date, remarks, status`; casts `status` boolean, `issued_date`/`received_date` to `date`; relation `delivery(): BelongsTo`; `scopeActive()`.
- Updated `App\Models\Delivery` — added `deliveryNote(): HasOne` (→ `DeliveryNote`).

Services

- Added `App\Services\DeliveryNoteService` — simplest service shape in the Sales module so far (no items to sync, since there's no items table): `create()` auto-generates `note_number` (`'DN-' . str_pad(DeliveryNote::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)` — the `DN-` prefix reserved for exactly this purpose back when Delivery Management's `DLV-` prefix was chosen), then a plain `DeliveryNote::create()`; `update()`/`delete()` are plain model calls.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\DeliveryNoteRequest` — `delivery_id` required `exists:deliveries,id` **and** `Rule::unique('delivery_notes', 'delivery_id')->ignore($id)` (app-level mirror of the DB's unique constraint, giving a friendly "This delivery already has a delivery note." message instead of a raw DB error, same technique used for Unit Conversion's `to_unit_id` and Product Prices' `price_tier_id`); `issued_date` required date; `received_by` nullable; `received_date` nullable `after_or_equal:issued_date`; `remarks` nullable; `status` required boolean.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\DeliveryNoteController` — index eager-loads the nested `delivery.salesOrder.customer` chain (no direct customer/order columns on `delivery_notes` itself); search matches `note_number`, `received_by`, or (via `orWhereHas`) the linked delivery's `delivery_number`. `create()` lists only `Delivery::active()->whereDoesntHave('deliveryNote')->get()` — deliveries that already have a note are excluded from the dropdown entirely, so the UI can't even present a choice that would fail the unique-constraint validation; `edit()` does the same `whereDoesntHave` filter **plus** the current record's own delivery (`->orWhere('id', $deliveryNote->delivery_id)`) so editing doesn't lose the currently-selected delivery from the list. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` wrapped in `DB::beginTransaction()`/`commit()`/`rollBack()` for consistency with every other module's controller shape in this codebase, even though this one has no child rows to keep in sync (confirmed via `CustomerController` that even single-table modules follow this transaction-wrapped convention here, not just master-detail ones). Added a `print(DeliveryNote $deliveryNote)` action — loads `delivery.salesOrder.customer` and `delivery.items.product`, returns a standalone (non-admin-layout) view, same "print utility" precedent as Product Management's Barcode Generator.

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/delivery-notes/{index,create,edit,action}.blade.php` — `'modal' => 'lg'` (a single delivery dropdown + a few plain fields, no repeatable item rows, so no need for the wider `'xl'` used by Sales Quotations/Orders). `action.blade.php` adds a third icon button — a "Print" link (`<a target="_blank">`, not an AJAX button) pointing at the new `admin.delivery-notes.print` route, alongside the usual Edit/Delete icons.
- Added `resources/views/admin/delivery-notes/print.blade.php` — a **complete standalone HTML document** (`<!doctype html>`...`</html>`, no `@extends` of the admin layout), following the exact Barcode Generator `print.blade.php` precedent: a small on-screen "Print" button hidden via `@media print { .print-actions { display: none } }`, a header box with order/delivery/customer/carrier/tracking info, a plain HTML items table (pulled from `$deliveryNote->delivery->items`, not a separate items source), an optional remarks paragraph, and a two-column "Delivered By / Received By" signature block (pre-filled with `received_by`/`received_date` when already set). No JS library added — same "no new dependency for one print screen" reasoning as Barcode Generator's `JsBarcode`-only-via-CDN choice, except here nothing beyond plain HTML/CSS was even needed.

JS

- Added `public/assets/system/js/pages/delivery-notes.js` — a plain single-table DataTable init/search/pagination/status-filter script, structurally identical to every simple-lookup module's JS in this project (no repeatable-row builder needed, since there are no line items on this form).

Route-model-binding param is `{delivery_note}`. Added `use App\Http\Controllers\Admin\DeliveryNoteController;` alongside the other Sales controller imports.

Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker per established precedent. No separate `.print` permission was added — printing is gated by the existing `.view` permission, same as how Barcode Generator's `print()` action needed no permission beyond `barcode-generator.view`.

### 2026-08-01 (10)

Completed

- Sales Invoices (tenth Sales module — the financial billing document, same header+line-items master-detail shape as Sales Quotations/Orders, with payment tracking added)

Database

- Added `sales_invoices`/`sales_invoice_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_180000_create_sales_invoices_table.php`), same shape as `sales_orders`/`sales_order_items`, plus payment fields:
  - `sales_invoices`: `invoice_number` unique (server-generated); `customer_id` required `foreignId` → `customers.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as every prior Sales header table — an invoice is meaningless without its customer); `sales_order_id` **nullable**, `nullOnDelete` (same "survives if the source is deleted" reasoning as `sales_orders.sales_quotation_id` — an issued invoice is an independent legal/financial record even if the originating order is later deleted, verified in testing); `payment_term_id` nullable, `nullOnDelete`; `invoice_date` required date, `due_date` nullable date (`after_or_equal:invoice_date`); `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only (same convention as Sales Quotations/Orders); `amount_paid` decimal(15,2) default 0 — a genuinely new field for this module, since Sales Quotations/Orders have no payment concept; `invoice_status` enum (`draft`/`sent`/`partially_paid`/`paid`/`overdue`/`cancelled`) — a **fourth distinct status enum** in the Sales module (different from `SalesQuotation::STATUSES`, `SalesOrder::STATUSES`, and `Delivery::STATUSES`), reflecting the invoice's own billing/collection lifecycle; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `sales_invoice_items`: identical shape to `sales_order_items`/`sales_quotation_items` (`sales_invoice_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`, `quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total` decimal fields). No unique constraint on `(sales_invoice_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table in this module.

Models

- Added `App\Models\SalesInvoice` — fillable `invoice_number, customer_id, sales_order_id, payment_term_id, invoice_date, due_date, subtotal, discount_total, grand_total, amount_paid, invoice_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','sent','partially_paid','paid','overdue','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `invoice_date`/`due_date` to `date`, all four money fields to `decimal:2`; relations `customer()`, `salesOrder()`, `paymentTerm()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `SalesInvoiceItem`); `scopeActive()`. **New pattern for this module**: `protected $appends = ['balance_due']` plus `getBalanceDueAttribute()` (`round($grand_total - $amount_paid, 2)`) — a computed accessor, **not a stored column**. Deliberate: `amount_paid` can be updated independently of the line items (e.g. recording a partial payment), and storing `balance_due` as a column would require remembering to recompute it on every `amount_paid` change outside of `syncItems()`'s totals recalculation — an accessor guarantees it's always correct from whatever `grand_total`/`amount_paid` currently are, with no separate write path to keep in sync.
- Added `App\Models\SalesInvoiceItem` — fillable `sales_invoice_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, discount, line_total`; casts all four numeric fields to `decimal:2`; relations `salesInvoice()`, `product()`.
- **No new relation was added on `SalesOrder`** (e.g. `salesInvoices(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning noted for the `SalesQuotation`↔`SalesOrder`/`SalesOrder`↔`Delivery` pairs in prior entries.

Services

### 2026-08-01 (12)

Completed

- Sales Returns (twelfth Sales module — the logistics/receiving side of a return: physical goods coming back from a customer, with per-item condition tracking; Credit Notes already covers the financial side)

Scope decision

- A return has **two sides**, already split across two modules per the roadmap: **Credit Notes** (just built) handles the financial side — how much money/credit the customer is owed. **Sales Returns** handles the logistics side — what physical goods came back, in what quantity, and in what condition (good/damaged/defective), optionally traced back to the originating Sales Order and/or Delivery. This is the same "financial document vs. logistics record" split already established between Sales Invoices and Delivery Management, applied to the return direction.
- **No pricing fields on this document** (same scope decision as Delivery Management) — `sales_return_items` has `quantity` + `condition` + a short `notes` field, no `unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total`. If a credit is owed for the return, that's created as a separate `CreditNote` referencing the same customer/invoice; the two records are linked only by shared context (customer/order), not a hard FK to each other — deliberately, since not every return results in a credit (e.g. a warranty replacement) and not every credit note originates from a physical return (e.g. a pricing correction), so forcing a FK between them would misrepresent cases that don't fit that 1:1 assumption.

Database

- Added `sales_returns`/`sales_return_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_200000_create_sales_returns_table.php`):
  - `sales_returns`: `return_number` unique (server-generated); `customer_id` required `foreignId` → `customers.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as every prior Sales header table); `sales_order_id` **nullable**, `nullOnDelete`; `delivery_id` **nullable**, `nullOnDelete` (both optional source-document links, same "survives if the source is deleted" reasoning as every other optional FK in this module — a return record remains valid even if the order/delivery it references is later removed, verified in testing for both); `return_date` required date; `reason` nullable string (same "short free-text label, no dedicated lookup table" scope decision as Credit Notes' `reason`); `return_status` enum (`pending`/`received`/`inspected`/`completed`/`cancelled`) — a **sixth distinct status enum** in the Sales module, modeling the physical intake workflow (received → inspected → completed) rather than a financial or delivery-tracking lifecycle; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `sales_return_items`: `sales_return_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as every prior line-item table); `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; **`condition` enum (`good`/`damaged`/`defective`) default `good`** — a genuinely new column shape for this module, since no prior Sales line-item table needed to record the physical state of the returned goods (Delivery Management only tracks what was shipped, not what came back or in what state); `notes` nullable string (per-line remark, e.g. "box crushed", distinct from the header's own `notes`). No unique constraint on `(sales_return_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table.

Models

- Added `App\Models\SalesReturn` — fillable `return_number, customer_id, sales_order_id, delivery_id, return_date, reason, return_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['pending','received','inspected','completed','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `return_date` to `date`; relations `customer()`, `salesOrder()`, `delivery()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `SalesReturnItem`); `scopeActive()`. No `$table` override needed — Laravel's default pluralization of `SalesReturn` already resolves to `sales_returns` correctly.
- Added `App\Models\SalesReturnItem` — fillable `sales_return_id, product_id, quantity, condition, notes`; `public const CONDITIONS = ['good','damaged','defective']` (single source of truth for the Form Request's `Rule::in()`, same technique as every other enum constant in this project); casts `quantity` to `decimal:2`; relations `salesReturn()`, `product()`.
- **No new relations were added on `SalesOrder`/`Delivery`** (e.g. `salesReturns(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning noted for every prior Sales document pair in this sequence.

Services

- Added `App\Services\SalesReturnService` — same delete-then-recreate `syncItems()` shape as Delivery Management's service (no totals to compute, since there's no pricing on this document): `generateReturnNumber()` — `'RET-' . str_pad(SalesReturn::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, a new `RET-` prefix, distinct from every other Sales document prefix in this project (`SQ-`/`SO-`/`DLV-`/`DN-`/`INV-`/`CN-`/CRM's `QUO-`). `syncItems()` writes `condition` (defaulting to `'good'` if omitted) and `notes` per item alongside `product_id`/`quantity`.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\SalesReturnRequest` — `customer_id` required `exists:customers,id`; `sales_order_id`/`delivery_id` both nullable `exists:` checks; `return_date` required date; `reason` nullable string; `return_status` required `Rule::in(SalesReturn::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1`; `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id`; `items.*.quantity` required numeric `min:0.01`; `items.*.condition` required `Rule::in(SalesReturnItem::CONDITIONS)`; `items.*.notes` nullable string. No price/discount rules, matching the schema.

Controllers

DataTable's `return_number` column subtitles the customer name, `return_status_badge` has its own 5-way color map (`received` → info, `inspected` → warning, `completed` → success, `cancelled` → danger). `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as every prior master-detail module.

### 2026-08-01 (13)

Completed

- POS System (thirteenth Sales module — a live checkout terminal for fast in-person sales, plus a read-only sales history)

Scope decision — deliberate UI deviation from the standard modal-CRUD pattern

- Every prior Sales module (and nearly every module in this project) follows the same "index list + create/edit modal" shape. A real point-of-sale screen cannot follow that shape — a cashier building a cart and checking out is a live, single-page interaction (click products, adjust quantities, take payment, print a receipt), not a form submitted inside a Bootstrap modal. This is the same category of deliberate deviation already established twice before in this project (Opportunities' Kanban board, Barcode Generator's print workflow) — a genuinely different interaction model, not a stylistic choice.
- Concretely, this means: **no `Route::resource`**, **no create/edit modal views**, **no `.js` repeatable-row builder**. Instead: a `terminal` screen (product grid + cart, full custom UI) that POSTs directly to a `checkout` endpoint creating a complete `PosSale` record in one shot, and a separate read-only `index` history list (standard DataTable, matching every other module's list-screen conventions) with **void** (not edit) and **receipt print** actions per row — a completed sale's line items are never edited after the fact, only voided, since editing a real transaction's contents after checkout would misrepresent what actually happened at the register.
- **No inventory/stock deduction** — the Inventory module (roadmap item 6) doesn't exist yet, so POS checkout does not decrement any stock quantity; this is purely a sales-recording feature for now, consistent with every other Sales module in this project not touching inventory (none of them do, since Inventory hasn't been built).

Database

- Added `pos_sales`/`pos_sale_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_210000_create_pos_sales_table.php`):
  - `pos_sales`: `pos_number` unique (server-generated); `customer_id` **nullable**, `nullOnDelete` — **the first Sales header table in this sequence where the customer FK is optional**, since walk-in POS sales commonly have no registered customer at all (every prior Sales document required a real `Customer`); `cashier_id` nullable `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `nullOnDelete` (which admin operated the terminal, auto-set server-side from `auth()->guard('admin')->id()`, never client-submitted); `sold_at` datetime (not just a date, unlike every other Sales document — a POS sale is a point-in-time event, precise to the minute, auto-set to `now()` at checkout); `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only; `payment_method` enum (`cash`/`card`/`bank_transfer`/`other`) default `cash`; `amount_tendered` nullable decimal (how much cash/card the customer handed over); `change_due` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed as `max(0, amount_tendered - grand_total)`; `pos_status` enum (`completed`/`voided`) — a **seventh distinct status enum** in the Sales module, the simplest of all of them since a POS sale only ever has two states; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean (the usual active/inactive archive toggle, independent of `pos_status`).
  - `pos_sale_items`: identical shape to `sales_invoice_items` (`pos_sale_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`, `quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total` decimal fields). No unique constraint on `(pos_sale_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table.

Models

### 2026-08-01 (14)

Completed

- Sales Targets (fourteenth Sales module — assign a revenue target to a salesperson for a period, track actual vs. target)
- **Plus a necessary retrofit**: added `assigned_to` (salesperson) to `sales_orders` and `sales_invoices` — required infrastructure this module depends on, not scope creep (explained below).

Scope decision — why the retrofit was necessary

- A sales target only means something if it can be measured against real sales attributed to that salesperson. Checked every existing Sales document (`SalesQuotation`, `SalesOrder`, `SalesInvoice`, `Delivery`, `CreditNote`, `SalesReturn`, `PosSale`) for anything resembling a salesperson/owner column — **none existed** except `PosSale.cashier_id` (which records who operated the register, not who "owns" the sale relationship). Building "Sales Targets" without fixing this gap would have produced a module that could never compute a real achievement figure.
- Followed the exact "build the dependency, then retrofit the FK" pattern already used repeatedly in this project (Departments/Designations, Products/Product Variants, Customer Groups → `customers.customer_group_id`, Payment Terms → `customers.payment_term_id`): two small follow-up migrations add `assigned_to` (nullable `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `nullOnDelete`) to `sales_orders` and `sales_invoices`, positioned `->after('customer_id')`. Chose **Sales Orders** as the metric to measure targets against (not Invoices) — a target is naturally about sales *made*, and an order is created at the point of sale; an invoice can lag behind (or never get issued for an order that's still processing). `sales_invoices.assigned_to` was still added for consistency/reporting completeness even though `SalesTarget::achieved_amount` currently only reads from `SalesOrder`.
- This is the **only** existing-module modification made in this task, and it's the same kind of carve-out explicitly permitted by this project's standing instructions ("Do not modify existing modules unless required for the current module... e.g. retrofitting a FK per the build dependency, then retrofit pattern already used repeatedly").

Database (retrofit)

- Added `database/migrations/2026_08_01_220000_add_assigned_to_to_sales_orders_table.php` and `..._220001_add_assigned_to_to_sales_invoices_table.php` — each adds `assigned_to` nullable `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `nullOnDelete`, positioned `->after('customer_id')`.

### 2026-08-01 (15)

Completed

- Sales Commission (fifteenth Sales module — calculates commission earned by a salesperson from their sales in a period, with a payment lifecycle)

Scope decision — snapshot vs. live computation

- Reused the `assigned_to`/`SalesOrder` attribution infrastructure retrofitted for Sales Targets in the previous task — no further schema changes needed on `sales_orders`. However, unlike `SalesTarget::achieved_amount` (a **live-computed** accessor, recalculated fresh every time it's read), Sales Commission **snapshots** `sales_amount`/`commission_amount` into real columns at calculation time. Reasoning: a target is a forward-looking goal an admin might check progress against at any moment, so "always fresh" is the right behavior; a commission is closer to a payroll record — once calculated (and especially once marked paid), it represents money that either has been or is about to be paid out, and must not silently change if the underlying orders are edited or cancelled afterward. This mirrors HRM's own `Payroll` precedent exactly (a stored snapshot, not a live figure) rather than the `SalesTarget` precedent from the immediately preceding task — a deliberate, explained divergence between two otherwise similar-looking modules.
- Followed the **Payroll** module's naming/workflow convention closely (checked `PayrollController`/`Payroll` model directly before building): `payment_status` (not `pos_status`-style custom naming), `payment_date`, a dedicated `markAsPaid()` service method + `mark-paid` route/permission (not a generic `.edit`), and a server-side guard rejecting `update()` once `payment_status === 'paid'` (Payroll's equivalent is stricter — it has no `.edit` permission at all, only generate/delete — Sales Commission is slightly more permissive, allowing edits **before** payment, since a commission's rate/period might reasonably need correcting before it's finalized, but once paid it's locked exactly like Payroll's records).

- Added `sales_commissions` (`database/migrations/2026_08_01_240000_create_sales_commissions_table.php`): `admin_id` required `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as `sales_targets.admin_id`); `period_type` enum (`monthly`/`quarterly`/`yearly`) default `monthly`, reusing the exact same 3 values as `SalesTarget::PERIOD_TYPES` (not the same constant/shared enum — each model defines its own, consistent with this project's per-model `STATUSES`-constant convention, but conceptually the same cadence options); `period_start`/`period_end` dates; `commission_rate` decimal(5,2) — a percentage (e.g. `5.00` = 5%), capped `0.01`-`100` at the Form Request level; `sales_amount`/`commission_amount` decimal(15,2) default 0 — **stored snapshots**, computed once at create/update time, not accessors; `payment_status` enum (`pending`/`paid`) default `pending` — a **ninth distinct status-style enum** in the Sales module, the simplest binary one; `payment_date` nullable date, set only by `markAsPaid()`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean. `unique(['admin_id', 'period_start', 'period_end'], 'sc_admin_period_unique')` — same one-record-per-exact-period guarantee as `sales_targets`, independently enforced (a salesperson's target and commission records for the same period are two separate rows in two separate tables, not linked to each other — a commission doesn't need to reference a specific target to exist).

Models

- Added `App\Models\SalesCommission` — fillable `admin_id, period_type, period_start, period_end, commission_rate, sales_amount, commission_amount, payment_status, payment_date, notes, status`; `public const PERIOD_TYPES`/`PAYMENT_STATUSES`; casts `status` boolean, `period_start`/`period_end`/`payment_date` to `date`, `commission_rate`/`sales_amount`/`commission_amount` to `decimal:2`; relation `admin(): BelongsTo`; `scopeActive()`. No accessor — unlike `SalesTarget`, the figures are real stored columns.

Services

- Added `App\Services\SalesCommissionService` — `create()`/`update()` both funnel through a shared `calculateAmounts()` helper (reuses the same `SalesOrder::where('assigned_to', ...)->where('order_status', '!=', 'cancelled')->whereBetween('order_date', [...])->sum('grand_total')` query `SalesTarget::getAchievedAmountAttribute()` established, but here the result is written into `$data['sales_amount']` before the model is saved, not returned as a live accessor value) then computes `commission_amount = round(sales_amount * (commission_rate / 100), 2)`. `markAsPaid()` — a small dedicated method (same shape as `PayrollController`'s `markAsPaid`/`OpportunityService::updateStage()`) that sets `payment_status = 'paid'` and `payment_date = now()`. `delete()` is a plain model delete.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\SalesCommissionRequest` — `admin_id` required `exists:admins,id`; `period_type` required `Rule::in(SalesCommission::PERIOD_TYPES)`; `period_start` required date; `period_end` required date `after_or_equal:period_start`; `commission_rate` required numeric `min:0.01` `max:100`; `notes`/`status` standard. Same `withValidator()` duplicate-period closure technique as `SalesTargetRequest`, adapted to this table/route-param. `sales_amount`/`commission_amount`/`payment_status`/`payment_date` are all absent from the rules — the first two are server-computed, the latter two are only ever set via the dedicated `mark-paid` endpoint, never through the create/edit form.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\SalesCommissionController` — index eager-loads `admin`, adds `admin_id`/`payment_status` AJAX filters, search matches the salesperson's `name`. DataTable columns: `admin_name` (name + period-type + rate subtitle), `period_label`, `sales_amount_formatted`, `commission_amount_formatted`, `payment_status_badge` (green "Paid (date)" or grey "Pending", same visual idiom as Payroll's payment-status badge), `status_badge`. **`update()` includes a server-side guard**: if `payment_status === 'paid'`, the request is rejected with a 422 and a clear message ("A paid commission cannot be edited.") before any service call — enforced at the controller, not just hidden in the UI, so a paid record genuinely cannot be altered through this endpoint regardless of what the client sends. Added `markAsPaid()` action (no Form Request needed, just the route-model-bound record).

### 2026-08-02 (3)

Completed

- Vendor Performance (third Purchase module — a periodic manual evaluation record rating a vendor across quality, delivery, pricing, and communication)

Scope decision

- Purchase Orders/Goods Receipts (the transactional records a "real" auto-computed vendor performance metric would need) don't exist yet — they're later items in the same roadmap section. Rather than defer this checklist item or build something that can't yet compute anything real, this module follows the exact precedent HRM's own **Performance Reviews** module already established for Employees: a periodic, manually-entered evaluation record (not a live-computed metric), reviewed by an admin, scoped to a date range, with an overall score derived from sub-scores. When Purchase Orders/Goods Receipts are eventually built, an auto-computed on-time-delivery-rate or defect-rate metric could be added as a *separate* future enhancement — this module doesn't block that, it just doesn't invent transactional data that doesn't exist yet.
- Checked `PerformanceReview`'s exact shape first (`employee_id`/`reviewer_id`/`review_period_start`/`review_period_end`/`rating`) and mirrored it closely, renamed for vendors and expanded from a single `rating` to four sub-scores (`quality_rating`/`delivery_rating`/`pricing_rating`/`communication_rating`) plus a computed `overall_rating` — a deliberate expansion since a vendor evaluation genuinely has multiple independent axes (unlike the single overall employee rating), not over-engineering.

Database

- Added `vendor_performance_reviews` (`database/migrations/2026_08_02_110000_create_vendor_performance_reviews_table.php`): `vendor_id` required `foreignId` → `vendors.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (a review has no meaning without the vendor it evaluates, same reasoning as `performance_reviews.employee_id`); `reviewed_by` nullable `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `nullOnDelete` (the reviewer is optional/attributable, same as `performance_reviews.reviewer_id`); `review_period_start`/`review_period_end` dates; `quality_rating`/`delivery_rating`/`pricing_rating`/`communication_rating` decimal(3,1) default 0 (0-5 scale each, validated at the Form Request level); `overall_rating` decimal(3,1) default 0 — **server-computed and stored** (the average of the four sub-scores), same "stored snapshot, not a live accessor" choice as Sales Commission, since there's no live transactional data this could instead be derived from; `remarks` nullable text; `status` boolean.

Models

- Added `App\Models\VendorPerformanceReview` — fillable `vendor_id, reviewed_by, review_period_start, review_period_end, quality_rating, delivery_rating, pricing_rating, communication_rating, overall_rating, remarks, status`; casts `status` boolean, both period dates to `date`, all five rating fields to `decimal:1`; relations `vendor(): BelongsTo`, `reviewedBy(): BelongsTo` (→ `Admin` via `reviewed_by`, non-default relation name, same pattern as `SalesOrder::assignedTo()`); `scopeActive()`.
- **No new relation was added on `Vendor`** (e.g. `performanceReviews(): HasMany`) — not needed by anything built in this task, same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project; trivial to add later if a future "review history per vendor" view needs it.

Services

- Added `App\Services\VendorPerformanceReviewService` — `create()`/`update()` both call a shared `calculateOverallRating()` helper (averages the four submitted sub-scores, rounds to 1 decimal) before writing the row, so `overall_rating` is always derived fresh from whatever sub-scores were just submitted — no drift risk between the sub-scores and the stored average, since both are written from the same request in the same call. `delete()` is a plain model delete.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\VendorPerformanceReviewRequest` — `vendor_id` required `exists:vendors,id`; `reviewed_by` nullable `exists:admins,id`; `review_period_start` required date; `review_period_end` required date `after_or_equal:review_period_start`; all four rating fields required numeric `min:0` `max:5`; `remarks`/`status` standard. `overall_rating` deliberately absent — server-computed only, never client-submitted.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\VendorPerformanceReviewController` — index eager-loads `vendor`/`reviewedBy`, adds a `vendor_id` AJAX filter, search matches the vendor's `name` via `whereHas`, default sort `review_period_start DESC` (most recent review period first, same chronological-sort reasoning as Relationship History/Activities from CRM). DataTable columns: `vendor_name` (name + reviewer subtitle), `period_label`, `overall_rating_badge` (color-coded: ≥4 → success, ≥2.5 → warning, else danger — a new "star rating badge" idiom, distinct from the percentage-based `achievement_badge` used by Sales Targets), `status_badge`. Standard CRUD shape otherwise, no items to sync.

Views

### 2026-08-02 (4)

Completed

- Purchase Requests (fourth Purchase module — an internal requisition for products to be purchased, header + line items, no pricing yet)

Scope decision

- A Purchase Request is the first step in the purchasing chain, submitted *before* any vendor/price is known — pricing and vendor selection happen later at the RFQ/Supplier Quotation/Purchase Order stage (all separate, not-yet-built roadmap items). ### 2026-08-02 (6)

Completed

- RFQ Management (sixth Purchase module — a Request for Quotation document generated with reference to an approved Purchase Request, sent to one or more Vendors)

Scope decision

- Inspected `PurchaseRequest`/`PurchaseRequestItem`/`PurchaseRequestService`/`PurchaseRequestController` directly before starting. An RFQ is conceptually "take a (usually approved) Purchase Request's need for products and ask multiple vendors to quote on it" — so it needed two relationships beyond a normal header+items document: an optional link back to its originating `PurchaseRequest`, and a many-to-many link to the `Vendor`s it was sent to (an RFQ is, almost by definition, sent to more than one vendor so their quotes can be compared — "Supplier Quotations", the very next roadmap item, will be the vendor-side responses captured against this same RFQ).
- **No pricing fields** on `rfq_items` (same scope decision as Delivery Management/Sales Returns/Purchase Requests) — an RFQ *asks* for a price, it doesn't record one; `product_id` + `quantity` + a per-line `notes` field only. Actual vendor-quoted prices belong to the next module (Supplier Quotations), which will presumably reference `rfq_id` + `vendor_id` and add real pricing — this module intentionally stops short of that.
- **`purchase_request_id` is nullable, `nullOnDelete`** (not `cascadeOnDelete`) — same "survives if the source document is deleted" reasoning used repeatedly for optional source-document FKs in Sales (`sales_orders.sales_quotation_id`, `sales_invoices.sales_order_id`, `credit_notes.sales_invoice_id`): an RFQ that has already been sent to vendors is a real, independent business record even if the originating Purchase Request is later deleted, verified in testing. It's nullable (not required) since an RFQ can also be created ad hoc without going through the Purchase Request approval flow, e.g. for a routine re-quote.
- **Vendor selection modeled as a genuine pivot table (`rfq_vendors`), not a plain array column** — because each vendor relationship on an RFQ needs its own tracked state (`sent_status`: pending/sent/responded/declined), which the next module (Supplier Quotations) will presumably update per vendor as responses come in. This is the same "real many-to-many table, not a comma-separated column" decision already made for Product Variants' `product_variant_attribute_values` pivot. `RfqService::syncVendors()` preserves each vendor's existing `sent_status` across an edit (looked up by `vendor_id` before the delete-then-recreate) rather than resetting every vendor back to `pending` on every save — a small refinement beyond the plain delete-then-recreate convention, necessary here because (unlike bundle/price-list items, which have no independent state) a vendor's `sent_status` is meaningful data that an edit to the item list or header shouldn't silently discard.

Database

- Added `rfqs`/`rfq_items`/`rfq_vendors` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_02_130000_create_rfqs_table.php`):
  - `rfqs`: `rfq_number` unique (server-generated); `purchase_request_id` nullable `foreignId` → `purchase_requests.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `rfq_date` required date; `due_date` nullable date (`after_or_equal:rfq_date` at the Form Request level); `rfq_status` enum (`draft`/`sent`/`closed`/`cancelled`) default `draft` — a distinct status enum from every Purchase/Sales module's own lifecycle enum, modeling this document's own draft→sent→closed cycle; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `rfq_items`: `rfq_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete` (same reasoning as every prior line-item table in this project — a line has no meaning without its parent RFQ or the product it references); `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; `notes` nullable string. No unique constraint on `(rfq_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as Purchase Requests/Sales documents — a product could appear on multiple lines with different notes.
  - `rfq_vendors`: `rfq_id`/`vendor_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `sent_status` enum (`pending`/`sent`/`responded`/`declined`) default `pending` — the per-vendor state this module tracks, distinct from `rfq_status`'s document-level state; named unique index `rfq_vendor_unique` on the pair (custom short name, same MySQL-identifier-length reasoning as `pv_av_unique`/`pb_product_unique`/`pl_product_unique` from earlier sessions), preventing the same vendor being added twice to one RFQ.

Models

- Added `App\Models\Rfq` — fillable `rfq_number, purchase_request_id, rfq_date, due_date, rfq_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','sent','closed','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `rfq_date`/`due_date` to `date`; relations `purchaseRequest(): BelongsTo`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `RfqItem`), `rfqVendors(): HasMany` (→ `RfqVendor`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\RfqItem` — fillable `rfq_id, product_id, quantity, notes`; casts `quantity` to `decimal:2`; relations `rfq()`, `product()`.
- Added `App\Models\RfqVendor` — fillable `rfq_id, vendor_id, sent_status`; `public const SENT_STATUSES = ['pending','sent','responded','declined']`; relations `rfq()`, `vendor()`.
- **No new relation was added on `PurchaseRequest`** (e.g. `rfqs(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project for every optional source-document FK pair; trivial to add later if a future "RFQs generated from this request" view needs it.

Services

- Added `App\Services\RfqService` — same delete-then-recreate `syncItems()` shape as Purchase Requests' service (no totals to compute, since there's no pricing on this document): `generateRfqNumber()` — `'RFQ-' . str_pad(Rfq::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, a new `RFQ-` prefix, distinct from every other document reference number in this project (`PR-`/`VEN-`/`SQ-`/`SO-`/`DLV-`/`DN-`/`INV-`/`CN-`/`RET-`/`POS-`/CRM's `QUO-`). Added `syncVendors()` — the module's one piece of genuinely new logic: reads each existing `RfqVendor`'s `sent_status` keyed by `vendor_id` before deleting all rows, then recreates one row per submitted `vendor_id`, restoring its previous `sent_status` if it already existed (defaulting to `'pending'` for a newly-added vendor) — preserving per-vendor response tracking across header/item edits instead of resetting it.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\RfqRequest` — `purchase_request_id` nullable `exists:purchase_requests,id`; `rfq_date` required date; `due_date` nullable `after_or_equal:rfq_date`; `rfq_status` required `Rule::in(Rfq::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1` with `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id` and `items.*.quantity` required numeric `min:0.01`; `vendor_ids` required array `min:1` with `vendor_ids.*` `distinct` `exists:vendors,id` and a custom message ("Select at least one vendor to send this RFQ to.") tailored to the checkbox-list UX. No price/discount rules, matching the schema.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\RfqController` — index eager-loads `purchaseRequest` and `withCount(['items', 'rfqVendors'])`; adds `purchase_request_id`/`rfq_status` AJAX filters; search matches `rfq_number` or (via `orWhereHas`) the source purchase request's `request_number`. ### 2026-08-02 (7)

Completed

- Supplier Quotations (seventh Purchase module — captures a vendor's quoted prices in response to an RFQ, header + line items with real pricing)

Scope decision

- Inspected `Rfq`/`RfqVendor`/`RfqService` directly before starting. RFQ Management's own changelog entry explicitly flagged that "Supplier Quotations... will presumably reference `rfq_id` + `vendor_id` and add real pricing" and that `RfqVendor.sent_status` would be "updated per vendor as responses come in" by this module — both of those predictions are implemented here.
- `rfq_id` is **nullable, `nullOnDelete`** (same "survives if the source RFQ is deleted" reasoning as every optional source-document FK in this project) — a supplier quotation can also be captured ad hoc without a formal RFQ (e.g. a vendor proactively sends a price list). `vendor_id` is **required, `cascadeOnDelete`** — a quotation with no vendor is meaningless, same reasoning as every required parent-owns-child FK in this project (e.g. `sales_invoices.customer_id`).
- **Real pricing fields** on `supplier_quotation_items` (`quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total`), unlike RFQ's own item table which deliberately had none — this is exactly the module where vendor-quoted prices get recorded, so the Sales Quotation/Sales Order-style master-detail-with-pricing shape (`SalesQuotationService`'s `calculateTotals()`/`syncItems()` pattern) was reused here rather than the no-pricing shape used by Purchase Requests/RFQs.
- **New integration logic, not present in any prior master-detail service**: `SupplierQuotationService::markRfqVendorResponded()` — when a quotation is created/updated against an `rfq_id`+`vendor_id` pair, the matching `RfqVendor` row's `sent_status` is flipped to `'responded'` directly (a plain `RfqVendor::where(...)->update(...)` call, not routed through `RfqService`, since this is a one-column side effect on a table Supplier Quotations doesn't otherwise own). This closes the loop RFQ Management's own service (`RfqService::syncVendors()`) was built to preserve across edits.
- `quotation_status` is a distinct 4-value enum (`received`/`selected`/`rejected`/`expired`) from every other Purchase/Sales status enum in this project, modeling this document's own vendor-comparison lifecycle — `selected` is the status a future Purchase Orders module will presumably read to know which vendor's quotation to convert into a PO (not implemented here, out of scope for this task).

Database

- Added `supplier_quotations`/`supplier_quotation_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_02_140000_create_supplier_quotations_table.php`):
  - `supplier_quotations`: `quotation_number` unique (server-generated); `rfq_id` nullable `foreignId` → `rfqs.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `vendor_id` required `foreignId` → `vendors.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `quotation_date` required date; `valid_until` nullable date (`after_or_equal:quotation_date` at the Form Request level); `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only (same convention as every Sales financial document); `quotation_status` enum (`received`/`selected`/`rejected`/`expired`) default `received`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `supplier_quotation_items`: `supplier_quotation_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total` decimal(15,2) fields, identical shape to `sales_quotation_items`. No unique constraint on `(supplier_quotation_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table — a product could appear on multiple lines (e.g. tiered quantity pricing from the same vendor).

Models

- Added `App\Models\SupplierQuotation` — fillable `quotation_number, rfq_id, vendor_id, quotation_date, valid_until, subtotal, discount_total, grand_total, quotation_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['received','selected','rejected','expired']`; casts `status` boolean, `quotation_date`/`valid_until` to `date`, the three money fields to `decimal:2`; relations `rfq()`, `vendor()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `SupplierQuotationItem`); `scopeActive()`.

- **No new relation was added on `Rfq`** (e.g. `supplierQuotations(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project for every optional source-document FK pair; trivial to add later if a future "quotations received for this RFQ" view needs it.

Services

### 2026-08-02 (8)

Completed

- Purchase Orders (eighth Purchase module — the formal order placed with a vendor, optionally traced back through Purchase Request → RFQ → Supplier Quotation)

Scope decision

- Inspected `SupplierQuotation`/`SupplierQuotationService`/`SalesOrder` directly before starting. A Purchase Order is the point where the purchasing chain built so far (Purchase Request → RFQ → Supplier Quotation) converges into a real commitment to buy — so it carries **three** optional source-document FKs (`purchase_request_id`, `rfq_id`, `supplier_quotation_id`), all nullable/`nullOnDelete` (a PO can also be created ad hoc without going through the full chain, and it remains a valid standalone record if any upstream document is later deleted — same "survives if the source is deleted" reasoning used for every optional source-document FK in this project, e.g. `sales_orders.sales_quotation_id`).
- **Real pricing fields** on `purchase_order_items` (`quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total`) — same `SalesOrder`/`SupplierQuotation` master-detail-with-pricing shape, since a PO is a priced commitment, not a request or an ask.
- **New integration logic, mirroring Supplier Quotations' own `markRfqVendorResponded()` precedent**: `PurchaseOrderService::markSupplierQuotationSelected()` — when a PO is created/updated against a `supplier_quotation_id`, that quotation's `quotation_status` is flipped to `'selected'` directly (a plain `SupplierQuotation::where(...)->update(...)` call). This is exactly the behavior Supplier Quotations' own changelog entry predicted a future Purchase Orders module would need ("`selected`... is the status a future Purchase Orders module will presumably read to know which vendor's quotation to convert into a PO").
- `order_status` is a **new, distinct** 5-value enum (`pending`/`confirmed`/`partially_received`/`completed`/`cancelled`) — not reused from `SalesOrder::STATUSES` (which has `processing` instead of `partially_received`) since a PO's lifecycle is receiving-goods-oriented, anticipating the very next roadmap module (Goods Receipts), which will presumably move a PO from `confirmed` → `partially_received` → `completed` as goods arrive. That receiving logic itself is **not** implemented here — out of scope for this task — the enum value only exists so Goods Receipts has something to update into.

### 2026-08-02 (9)

Completed

- Goods Receipts (ninth Purchase module — the logistics/receiving side of a Purchase Order: physical goods coming in from a vendor, with per-item received quantity and condition tracking)

Scope decision

- Inspected `PurchaseOrder`/`PurchaseOrderService` and, for the closest existing precedent, `SalesReturn`/`SalesReturnItem`/`SalesReturnService` directly before starting. A Goods Receipt is the "incoming" mirror of Sales' Delivery Management (outgoing) — it records what was physically received against a PO, not a financial document, so it follows the exact "no pricing fields, condition tracking instead" shape `SalesReturnItem` already established (`quantity`/`condition`/`notes`, no `unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total`).
- **`purchase_order_id` is required, `cascadeOnDelete`** (not nullable) — unlike every optional source-document FK used elsewhere in Purchase/Sales, a goods receipt has no meaning without the PO it's receiving against; there is no "ad hoc receipt with no PO" concept the way an ad hoc Supplier Quotation could exist without an RFQ. This is a deliberate, more restrictive choice than the pattern used elsewhere, made because the parent-child relationship here is a real logical dependency, not just a usual originating reference.
- **No direct `vendor_id` column** — same reasoning as `Delivery` having no direct `customer_id`: the vendor is reached via `$goodsReceipt->purchaseOrder->vendor`, avoiding a redundant denormalized FK that would need to always agree with the PO's own vendor.
- `receipt_status` reuses the exact same 5-value enum as `SalesReturn::STATUSES` (`pending`/`received`/`inspected`/`completed`/`cancelled`) — both model a physical-intake workflow (received → inspected → completed), so no new enum shape was invented; each model still defines its own `public const STATUSES` (per this project's per-model-constant convention), they just happen to share the same values.
- **Deliberately did not auto-update `PurchaseOrder.order_status`** (e.g. to `partially_received`/`completed`) when a receipt is recorded — checked whether any prior "logistics record against a header document" module in this project did this (Delivery Management vs. `SalesOrder.order_status`, Sales Returns vs. `SalesOrder`/`Delivery`) and confirmed **none** of them auto-update the parent's status; an admin manually sets the PO's own `order_status` via its own edit form, same as every other module in this project. Keeping this consistent avoids introducing a new class of side-effect not seen anywhere else, and avoids the complexity of reconciling partial-vs-full received quantities across possibly multiple receipts against one PO — a genuine "receiving reconciliation" feature, judged out of scope for this task and flagged here as a natural follow-up if the client asks for automatic PO status transitions later.

Database

- Added `goods_receipts`/`goods_receipt_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_02_160000_create_goods_receipts_table.php`):
  - `goods_receipts`: `receipt_number` unique (server-generated); `purchase_order_id` required `foreignId` → `purchase_orders.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `received_by` nullable `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `received_date` required date; `receipt_status` enum (`pending`/`received`/`inspected`/`completed`/`cancelled`) default `pending`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `goods_receipt_items`: `goods_receipt_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity_received` decimal(15,2) default 1; `condition` enum (`good`/`damaged`/`defective`) default `good`; `notes` nullable string (per-line remark, e.g. "2 boxes crushed"). No unique constraint on `(goods_receipt_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table — a product could appear on multiple lines with different conditions (e.g. part of a shipment good, part damaged).

Models

- **No new relation was added on `PurchaseOrder`** (e.g. `goodsReceipts(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project; trivial to add later if a future "receipts recorded against this PO" view needs it.

Services

### 2026-08-02 (10)

Completed

- Purchase Invoice Matching (tenth Purchase module — the vendor's billed invoice, financially closing the purchasing chain, with an automated 3-way match against the linked Purchase Order and Goods Receipt)

Scope decision

- Inspected `SalesInvoice` (for the payment/`balance_due` accessor shape) and `PurchaseOrder`/`GoodsReceipt` (for the match comparison data) directly before starting. This module is the Purchase-side counterpart to Sales Invoices — same header+items-with-pricing shape, `amount_paid`/`balance_due` accessor pattern (`SalesInvoice::getBalanceDueAttribute()` copied verbatim as `PurchaseInvoice::getBalanceDueAttribute()`) — but its defining feature, and the reason this checklist item is named "**Matching**" rather than just "Purchase Invoices", is a real automated 3-way match, not just a document.
- **Implemented an actual 3-way match, not a placeholder status field**: `PurchaseInvoiceService::calculateMatchStatus()` checks each invoiced line's **quantity** against what was actually received (`GoodsReceiptItem.quantity_received`, summed per product) when a Goods Receipt is linked — falling back to the Purchase Order's ordered quantity if no receipt is linked — and always checks invoiced **unit price** against the Purchase Order's agreed price when a PO is linked. Any mismatch (or a product on the invoice with no corresponding PO/GR line at all) sets `match_status = 'discrepancy'`; a clean match sets `'matched'`; and an invoice with neither a PO nor a GR linked (nothing to compare against) is `'unmatched'`. This is a genuinely new kind of service method for this project — every prior `calculateTotals()`/`syncItems()` pair just summed/wrote data; this one reads from **two other tables' line items** to validate a third.
- Both `purchase_order_id` and `goods_receipt_id` are **nullable, `nullOnDelete`** — an invoice can be recorded standalone (match_status then correctly reports `unmatched`), and remains a valid financial record if either linked source document is later deleted (re-verified `nullOnDelete` behavior, not `cascadeOnDelete`, since a billed invoice is not logically dependent on the survival of the PO/GR the way a receipt is dependent on its PO). `vendor_id` remains required/`cascadeOnDelete`, same reasoning as every required parent-owns-child FK in this project.
- `invoice_status` is a **new, distinct** 5-value enum (`pending`/`approved`/`paid`/`disputed`/`cancelled`) — not reused from `SalesInvoice::STATUSES` (which has `draft`/`sent`/`partially_paid`/`overdue` instead), since this is the vendor-payable side of the ledger with its own approval-then-pay lifecycle, plus a `disputed` value specifically for invoices flagged by the match engine that a human needs to resolve with the vendor.

Database

- Added `purchase_invoices`/`purchase_invoice_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_02_170000_create_purchase_invoices_table.php`):
  - `purchase_invoices`: `invoice_number` unique (server-generated); `vendor_id` required `foreignId` → `vendors.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `purchase_order_id`/`goods_receipt_id` both nullable `foreignId`s, `nullOnDelete`; `invoice_date` required date; `due_date` nullable date (`after_or_equal:invoice_date` at the Form Request level); `subtotal`/`discount_total`/`grand_total` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only; `amount_paid` decimal(15,2) default 0; `match_status` enum (`unmatched`/`matched`/`discrepancy`) default `unmatched`, server-computed only (never client-submitted, same "computed field absent from the Form Request rules" convention as `subtotal`/`grand_total`); `invoice_status` enum (`pending`/`approved`/`paid`/`disputed`/`cancelled`) default `pending`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `purchase_invoice_items`: `purchase_invoice_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity`/`unit_price`/`discount`/`line_total` decimal(15,2) fields, identical shape to `purchase_order_items`/`sales_invoice_items`. No unique constraint on `(purchase_invoice_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table in this project.

Models

- Added `App\Models\PurchaseInvoice` — fillable `invoice_number, vendor_id, purchase_order_id, goods_receipt_id, invoice_date, due_date, subtotal, discount_total, grand_total, amount_paid, match_status, invoice_status, notes, status`; `public const MATCH_STATUSES = ['unmatched','matched','discrepancy']` and `public const STATUSES = ['pending','approved','paid','disputed','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `invoice_date`/`due_date` to `date`, the four money fields to `decimal:2`; `protected $appends = ['balance_due']`; relations `vendor()`, `purchaseOrder()`, `goodsReceipt()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `PurchaseInvoiceItem`); `getBalanceDueAttribute()` (`round($grand_total - $amount_paid, 2)`, same accessor-not-column reasoning as `SalesInvoice`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\PurchaseInvoiceItem` — fillable `purchase_invoice_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, discount, line_total`; casts all four numeric fields to `decimal:2`; relations `purchaseInvoice()`, `product()`.
- **No new relations were added on `PurchaseOrder`/`GoodsReceipt`** (e.g. `purchaseInvoices(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project; trivial to add later if a future "invoices billed against this PO/receipt" view needs it.

Services

Added `calculateMatchStatus(?int $purchaseOrderId, ?int $goodsReceiptId, array $items): string` (described in the Scope decision above) — called from both `create()` and `update()`, writing its result into `match_status` before the header row is saved, so the match is always freshly recalculated against whatever the current PO/GR/items state is at save time (not a stale one-time check).

### 2026-08-02 (12)

Completed

- Purchase Returns (twelfth Purchase module — the logistics/receiving-reverse side of a return: physical goods being sent back to a vendor, with per-item condition tracking; Debit Notes already covers the financial side)

Scope decision

- Same "financial document vs. logistics record" split already established between Sales' Credit Notes and Sales Returns, applied here in the Purchase direction: **Debit Notes** (just built) handles the financial side — how much we're owed back / what's deducted from what we owe the vendor. **Purchase Returns** handles the logistics side — what physical goods are going back, in what quantity, and in what condition, optionally traced to the originating Purchase Order and/or Goods Receipt. Inspected `SalesReturn`/`SalesReturnItem`/`SalesReturnService` and (for the Purchase-side FK precedent) `GoodsReceipt` directly before starting and mirrored `SalesReturn`'s exact shape, adapted for the Purchase direction.
- **No pricing fields** on `purchase_return_items` (same scope decision as `SalesReturnItem`/`GoodsReceiptItem`/Purchase Requests/RFQs) — just `quantity` + `condition` + a per-line `notes` field. If a debit is owed for the return, that's a separate `DebitNote` referencing the same vendor/invoice; the two records are linked only by shared context, not a hard FK to each other — same reasoning `SalesReturn`/`CreditNote` already established (not every return produces a debit, e.g. a warranty replacement; not every debit note originates from a physical return, e.g. a pricing correction).
- Both `purchase_order_id` and `goods_receipt_id` are nullable, `nullOnDelete` — a return can reference either or both optional source documents, and remains a valid standalone record if either is later deleted (re-verified in testing for both, mirroring `SalesReturn.sales_order_id`/`delivery_id`). `vendor_id` remains required, `cascadeOnDelete`, same reasoning as every required parent-owns-child FK in this project.
- `return_status` is a **new, distinct** 5-value enum (`pending`/`approved`/`shipped`/`completed`/`cancelled`) — not reused from `SalesReturn::STATUSES` (`pending`/`received`/`inspected`/`completed`/`cancelled`), since the two returns move in opposite physical directions: a Sales Return is goods **coming in** from a customer (received → inspected workflow), while a Purchase Return is goods **going out** to a vendor (approved → shipped workflow) — the enum values reflect that outbound-shipment lifecycle instead.

- Added `purchase_returns`/`purchase_return_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_02_190000_create_purchase_returns_table.php`):

  - `purchase_return_items`: `purchase_return_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; `condition` enum (`good`/`damaged`/`defective`) default `good`; `notes` nullable string (per-line remark, distinct from the header's own `notes`). No unique constraint on `(purchase_return_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table in this project.

Models

- Added `App\Models\PurchaseReturnItem` — fillable `purchase_return_id, product_id, quantity, condition, notes`; `public const CONDITIONS = ['good','damaged','defective']` (single source of truth for the Form Request's `Rule::in()`, same technique as `SalesReturnItem::CONDITIONS`/`GoodsReceiptItem::CONDITIONS`); casts `quantity` to `decimal:2`; relations `purchaseReturn()`, `product()`.
- **No new relations were added on `PurchaseOrder`/`GoodsReceipt`** (e.g. `purchaseReturns(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project; trivial to add later if a future "returns generated against this order/receipt" view needs it.

Scope decision

- Checked the Naming/Table Conflict Guard and existing migrations first — no `warehouses` table existed anywhere in the codebase, no collision.
- **`code` is user-entered, not server-generated** — a deliberate departure from Vendors'/Customers' auto-generated `vendor_code`/`customer_code` precedent. ### 2026-08-03 (3)

Completed

- Stock Entry (third Inventory module — records products physically received into a warehouse, optionally traced back to a Purchase Goods Receipt)

Scope decision

- A Stock Entry is the Inventory-side landing point for goods that have arrived — most commonly via a completed Purchase `GoodsReceipt`, so `goods_receipt_id` is a nullable, `nullOnDelete` optional source-document FK (same "survives if the source is deleted" reasoning used repeatedly for optional source-document FKs throughout this project). It's nullable rather than required since stock can also enter a warehouse without a formal Purchase Goods Receipt (e.g. production output, a stock correction being logged as an addition) — the very "Reason" field exists for exactly that free-text explanation.
- `warehouse_id` is required, `cascadeOnDelete` — a stock entry has no meaning without the warehouse it's stocking, same reasoning as every required parent-owns-child FK in this project. `warehouse_location_id` is optional/`nullOnDelete` (a business may or may not track down to the aisle/rack level for a given entry).
- **Deliberately does not maintain any running stock balance.** Checked the roadmap order — "Inventory Transactions" is a later, separate checklist item, and (per its position after Stock Entry/Opening Stock/Adjustment/Transfer/Count) is presumably the unified ledger/balance mechanism that reads across all of these entry types. Building balance-tracking logic into Stock Entry now would be premature — this module only records *that* a receipt happened (product, quantity, and an optional `unit_cost` for future Stock Valuation use), not a computed on-hand quantity.
- **No pricing/totals document shape** — `unit_cost` is stored per line (nullable, since cost isn't always known/relevant at entry time) but there's no `calculateTotals()`/`grand_total` the way Sales/Purchase financial documents have; a stock entry is a movement record, not a priced document billed to anyone. Same "no totals to compute" service shape as Delivery Management/Purchase Requests/Goods Receipts.
- `entry_status` is a simple 3-value enum (`draft`/`posted`/`cancelled`) — `posted` marks an entry as finalized (once "Inventory Transactions" exists, it would presumably only read `posted` entries into the ledger); this module does not itself enforce or act on that distinction beyond storing it, since the ledger-reading logic doesn't exist yet.

Database

- Added `stock_entries`/`stock_entry_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_03_110000_create_stock_entries_table.php`):
  - `stock_entries`: `entry_number` unique (server-generated); `warehouse_id` required `foreignId` → `warehouses.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `warehouse_location_id` nullable `foreignId` → `warehouse_locations.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `goods_receipt_id` nullable `foreignId` → `goods_receipts.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `entry_date` required date; `reason` nullable string; `entry_status` enum (`draft`/`posted`/`cancelled`) default `draft`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `stock_entry_items`: `stock_entry_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; `unit_cost` decimal(15,2) **nullable** (unlike every Sales/Purchase pricing document's `unit_price`, which is always required — cost may genuinely be unknown for a stock movement); `notes` nullable string. No unique constraint on `(stock_entry_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table in this project.

Models

- Added `App\Models\StockEntry` — fillable `entry_number, warehouse_id, warehouse_location_id, goods_receipt_id, entry_date, reason, entry_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','posted','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `entry_date` to `date`; relations `warehouse()`, `warehouseLocation()`, `goodsReceipt()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `StockEntryItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\StockEntryItem` — fillable `stock_entry_id, product_id, quantity, unit_cost, notes`; casts `quantity`/`unit_cost` to `decimal:2`; relations `stockEntry()`, `product()`.
- **No new relations were added on `Warehouse`/`WarehouseLocation`/`GoodsReceipt`** (e.g. `stockEntries(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project; trivial to add later if a future "entries recorded against this warehouse/receipt" view needs it.

Services

- Added `App\Services\StockEntryService` — same delete-then-recreate `syncItems()` shape as Delivery Management's/Goods Receipts' services (no totals to compute): `generateEntryNumber()` — `'SE-' . str_pad(StockEntry::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, a new `SE-` prefix, the first Inventory-module document reference number in this project, distinct from every other prefix used so far.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\StockEntryRequest` — `warehouse_id` required `exists:warehouses,id`; `warehouse_location_id`/`goods_receipt_id` both nullable `exists:` checks; `entry_date` required date; `reason` nullable string; `entry_status` required `Rule::in(StockEntry::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1` with `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id`, `items.*.quantity` required numeric `min:0.01`, `items.*.unit_cost` **nullable** numeric `min:0` (not required, matching the schema), `items.*.notes` nullable string.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\StockEntryController` — index eager-loads `warehouse`/`warehouseLocation` and `withCount('items')`; adds `warehouse_id`/`entry_status` AJAX filters; search matches `entry_number` or the warehouse's `name`. DataTable's `entry_number` column subtitles the warehouse name, plus the specific location name when one was recorded (`$row->warehouse->name . ' · ' . $row->warehouseLocation->name` when present); `entry_status_badge` has its own 3-way color map (`draft` → secondary, `posted` → success, `cancelled` → danger). `create()`/`edit()` load active `Warehouse`s/`WarehouseLocation`s/`GoodsReceipt`s/`Product`s for the form's dropdown/item-builder needs. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as every prior master-detail module.

Views

No totals-preview logic, matching the schema.

Route-model-binding param is `{stock_entry}`. Added `use App\Http\Controllers\Admin\StockEntryController;` alongside the other Inventory controller imports.

### 2026-08-03 (4)

Completed

- Opening Stock (fourth Inventory module — records the initial stock balances for a warehouse when the ERP first starts tracking that location)

Scope decision

- Kept the same header+items master-detail shape as Stock Entry (a batch of initial balances is naturally entered together, per warehouse, in one sitting) — same `warehouse_id`/`warehouse_location_id` FK shape (required `cascadeOnDelete` on the warehouse, optional `nullOnDelete` on the specific location).
- **`unit_cost` is required here, unlike Stock Entry's nullable `unit_cost`** — a deliberate divergence documented explicitly since the two tables otherwise look identical. Reasoning: Stock Entry records an incoming movement where cost may not always be known at entry time (e.g. logging a production output), but Opening Stock's entire purpose is establishing the initial *valuation* baseline for each product in a warehouse — a baseline with no cost is not useful, so it's enforced as `required|numeric|min:0` at the Form Request level and `decimal(15,2) default 0` (not nullable) at the schema level.
- **No `goods_receipt_id`** (unlike Stock Entry) — an opening balance is by definition not sourced from any transactional document; it exists to record what was already on hand before the ERP started tracking anything, so there is no possible source-document link to make.
- Still deliberately does not maintain any running/live stock balance — same reasoning as Stock Entry: that computation belongs to the future "Inventory Transactions" ledger module, not to this one.

Database

- Added `opening_stocks`/`opening_stock_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_03_120000_create_opening_stocks_table.php`):
  - `opening_stocks`: `entry_number` unique (server-generated); `warehouse_id` required `foreignId` → `warehouses.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `warehouse_location_id` nullable `foreignId` → `warehouse_locations.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `opening_date` required date; `entry_status` enum (`draft`/`posted`/`cancelled`) default `draft`, same 3-value shape as `StockEntry::STATUSES`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `opening_stock_items`: `opening_stock_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; `unit_cost` decimal(15,2) default 0, **not nullable** (per the Scope decision above); `notes` nullable string. No unique constraint on `(opening_stock_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table in this project.

Models

- Added `App\Models\OpeningStock` — fillable `entry_number, warehouse_id, warehouse_location_id, opening_date, entry_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','posted','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `opening_date` to `date`; relations `warehouse()`, `warehouseLocation()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `OpeningStockItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\OpeningStockItem` — fillable `opening_stock_id, product_id, quantity, unit_cost, notes`; casts `quantity`/`unit_cost` to `decimal:2`; relations `openingStock()`, `product()`.
- **No new relations were added on `Warehouse`/`WarehouseLocation`** (e.g. `openingStocks(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project.

Services

Requests

Scope decision

- Same header+items shape and `warehouse_id`/`warehouse_location_id` FK pattern as Stock Entry/Opening Stock — required `cascadeOnDelete` on the warehouse, optional `nullOnDelete` on the specific location.
- **New per-line `adjustment_type` enum (`increase`/`decrease`)** — the one genuinely new field shape in this Inventory sub-sequence so far. A correction can go either direction on the same document (e.g. one line increasing a miscounted product while another decreases a damaged one), so the direction is recorded per line item, not once at the header level. Modeled on `SalesReturnItem`/`GoodsReceiptItem`'s `condition` enum precedent (a fixed-choice classifier per line, validated via `Rule::in()` against a model constant), just with a different two-value set specific to this module's purpose.
- `unit_cost` is **nullable**, matching Stock Entry's precedent (not Opening Stock's required precedent) — an adjustment is a correction to quantity first and foremost; a cost figure is useful for future Stock Valuation but not always known or relevant at the time a miscount or damage is logged.
- Same "no running balance maintained here" reasoning as Stock Entry/Opening Stock — the actual increase/decrease math against a live on-hand quantity is deferred to the future "Inventory Transactions" ledger module.

Database

- Added `stock_adjustments`/`stock_adjustment_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_03_130000_create_stock_adjustments_table.php`):
  - `stock_adjustments`: `adjustment_number` unique (server-generated); `warehouse_id` required `foreignId` → `warehouses.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `warehouse_location_id` nullable `foreignId` → `warehouse_locations.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `adjustment_date` required date; `reason` nullable string; `adjustment_status` enum (`draft`/`posted`/`cancelled`) default `draft`, same 3-value shape as `StockEntry`/`OpeningStock`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `stock_adjustment_items`: `stock_adjustment_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `adjustment_type` enum (`increase`/`decrease`) default `increase`; `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; `unit_cost` decimal(15,2) nullable (matching Stock Entry, not Opening Stock); `notes` nullable string. No unique constraint on `(stock_adjustment_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table — a product could legitimately appear twice (e.g. one line increasing a miscounted batch, another decreasing a damaged batch of the same product).

Models

- Added `App\Models\StockAdjustment` — fillable `adjustment_number, warehouse_id, warehouse_location_id, adjustment_date, reason, adjustment_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','posted','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `adjustment_date` to `date`; relations `warehouse()`, `warehouseLocation()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `StockAdjustmentItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\StockAdjustmentItem` — fillable `stock_adjustment_id, product_id, adjustment_type, quantity, unit_cost, notes`; `public const ADJUSTMENT_TYPES = ['increase','decrease']` (single source of truth for the Form Request's `Rule::in()`, same technique as every other enum constant in this project); casts `quantity`/`unit_cost` to `decimal:2`; relations `stockAdjustment()`, `product()`.
- **No new relations were added on `Warehouse`/`WarehouseLocation`** — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project.

Services

- Added `App\Services\StockAdjustmentService` — same delete-then-recreate `syncItems()` shape as `StockEntryService`/`OpeningStockService` (no header totals to compute): `generateAdjustmentNumber()` — `'ADJ-' . str_pad(StockAdjustment::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, a new `ADJ-` prefix, distinct from Stock Entry's `SE-` and Opening Stock's `OS-`.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\StockAdjustmentRequest` — `warehouse_id` required `exists:warehouses,id`; `warehouse_location_id` nullable `exists:warehouse_locations,id`; `adjustment_date` required date; `reason` nullable string; `adjustment_status` required `Rule::in(StockAdjustment::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1` with `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id`, `items.*.adjustment_type` required `Rule::in(StockAdjustmentItem::ADJUSTMENT_TYPES)`, `items.*.quantity` required numeric `min:0.01`, `items.*.unit_cost` nullable numeric `min:0`, `items.*.notes` nullable string.

Controllers

DataTable's `adjustment_number` column subtitles the warehouse name plus the specific location when recorded, same idiom as Stock Entry's/Opening Stock's list columns; `adjustment_status_badge` has the same 3-way color map as its Inventory siblings. `create()`/`edit()` load active `Warehouse`s/`WarehouseLocation`s/`Product`s. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as every prior master-detail module.

### 2026-08-03 (6)

Completed

- Stock Transfer (sixth Inventory module — moves stock from one warehouse/location to another)

Scope decision

- **First Inventory table with two FKs to the same parent table** — `from_warehouse_id`/`to_warehouse_id` both `foreignId('...')->constrained('warehouses')`, both required and `cascadeOnDelete`. Same technique already used elsewhere in this project for a dual-reference-to-one-table shape (e.g. `SalesReturn` referencing both `sales_order_id`/`delivery_id` on different tables — here it's the *same* table twice, so explicit non-default relation names were required: `fromWarehouse()`/`toWarehouse()` via `belongsTo(Warehouse::class, 'from_warehouse_id')` etc., same "explicit FK column, non-default relation name" pattern as `Lead::assignedTo()`/`PurchaseOrder::purchaseRequest()`.
- **New cross-field validation**: `from_warehouse_id` carries a `different:to_warehouse_id` rule — a transfer moving stock from a warehouse to itself is meaningless. This is the first `different:` rule used in this project (prior cross-field rules were all `after_or_equal:`/`required_if:`-style date/conditional rules); it's Laravel's own built-in rule, not custom logic.
- Both `from_warehouse_location_id`/`to_warehouse_location_id` are optional/`nullOnDelete`, same as every other warehouse-location FK in this Inventory sub-sequence.
- **No `unit_cost` on `stock_transfer_items`** (unlike Stock Entry/Opening Stock/Stock Adjustment) — a transfer moves the *same* stock between two locations of the same business; it doesn't change what that stock is worth, so there's no cost figure to record here. Items are just `product_id` + `quantity` + `notes`, the simplest line-item shape of any Inventory document so far.
- `transfer_status` is a **new, distinct** 4-value enum (`draft`/`in_transit`/`completed`/`cancelled`) — not reused from `StockEntry`/`OpeningStock`/`StockAdjustment`'s shared `draft`/`posted`/`cancelled` shape, since a transfer between two locations has a genuine "in transit" phase between being recorded and being received at the destination that a same-location entry/adjustment doesn't have.
- Same "no running balance maintained here" reasoning as every prior Inventory module — the actual decrement-at-source/increment-at-destination math is deferred to the future "Inventory Transactions" ledger module.

  - `stock_transfer_items`: `stock_transfer_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `quantity` decimal(15,2) default 1; `notes` nullable string. No unique constraint on `(stock_transfer_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table.

- **No new relations were added on `Warehouse`/`WarehouseLocation`** — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project.

Custom message for the `different:` rule ("Source and destination warehouses must be different.").
