### 2026-08-03 (7)

Completed

- Stock Count (seventh Inventory module — records a physical count of stock in a warehouse and the resulting variance against a recorded system quantity)

Scope decision

- No live stock balance table exists yet in this project (deliberately deferred to the future "Inventory Transactions" ledger, per every prior Inventory module's changelog entry), so there is nothing for a Stock Count to automatically compare against. Rather than fake or skip the comparison, `system_quantity` is a **nullable, manually-entered** field per line — an admin who happens to know the expected quantity can enter it for an immediate variance check; if left blank, the count is recorded with no comparison, which is the honest state of "we don't have a live balance yet."
- **New computed-not-stored accessor**: `StockCountItem::getVarianceAttribute()` returns `counted_quantity - system_quantity`, or `null` when no `system_quantity` was entered. This is the same "compute from what's stored, never persist a derivable figure" reasoning already used for `SalesInvoice::balance_due`/`PurchaseInvoice::balance_due`, applied here per-line-item rather than per-header — the first per-line (not per-document) computed accessor in this project.
- Same header shape as Stock Entry/Opening Stock/Stock Adjustment (`warehouse_id` required `cascadeOnDelete`, `warehouse_location_id` optional `nullOnDelete`) — a count is naturally scoped to one physical location per document.
- `count_status` is a **new 3-value enum** (`draft`/`completed`/`cancelled`) — deliberately worded `completed` rather than reusing `posted` (the wording every other Inventory document uses for "finalized"), since a physical count is described as being *completed*, not *posted*, in ordinary usage — a small, intentional wording choice, not a functional difference from the other 3-value enums in this sub-sequence.
- No `unit_cost` on this document — a count is purely a quantity reconciliation exercise, not concerned with valuation (that's Stock Valuation's future job).

Database

- Added `stock_counts`/`stock_count_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_03_150000_create_stock_counts_table.php`):
  - `stock_counts`: `count_number` unique (server-generated); `warehouse_id` required `foreignId` → `warehouses.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `warehouse_location_id` nullable `foreignId` → `warehouse_locations.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `count_date` required date; `count_status` enum (`draft`/`completed`/`cancelled`) default `draft`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `stock_count_items`: `stock_count_id`/`product_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; `system_quantity` decimal(15,2) **nullable** (per the Scope decision above); `counted_quantity` decimal(15,2) default 0, **required** at the Form Request level (the actual count is always known — it's what's being recorded); `notes` nullable string. No unique constraint on `(stock_count_id, product_id)`, same reasoning as every prior line-item table.

Models

- Added `App\Models\StockCount` — fillable `count_number, warehouse_id, warehouse_location_id, count_date, count_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','completed','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `count_date` to `date`; relations `warehouse()`, `warehouseLocation()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `StockCountItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\StockCountItem` — fillable `stock_count_id, product_id, system_quantity, counted_quantity, notes`; casts `system_quantity`/`counted_quantity` to `decimal:2`; `protected $appends = ['variance']`; relations `stockCount()`, `product()`; `getVarianceAttribute()` (described in the Scope decision above).
- **No new relations were added on `Warehouse`/`WarehouseLocation`** — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project.

Services

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\StockCountRequest` — `warehouse_id` required `exists:warehouses,id`; `warehouse_location_id` nullable `exists:warehouse_locations,id`; `count_date` required date; `count_status` required `Rule::in(StockCount::STATUSES)`; `items` required array `min:1` with `items.*.product_id` required `distinct` `exists:products,id`, `items.*.system_quantity` **nullable** numeric `min:0` (matching the schema — the one genuinely optional numeric quantity field in this Inventory sub-sequence), `items.*.counted_quantity` required numeric `min:0`, `items.*.notes` nullable string.

Controllers

DataTable's `count_number` column subtitles the warehouse name plus location when recorded, same idiom as its Inventory siblings; `count_status_badge` has its own 3-way color map (`draft` → secondary, `completed` → success, `cancelled` → danger). `create()`/`edit()` load active `Warehouse`s/`WarehouseLocation`s/`Product`s. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as every prior master-detail module.

Views

### 2026-08-03 (8)

Completed

- Batch Management (eighth Inventory module — tracks batch/lot numbers per product per warehouse, with manufacturing/expiry dates and quantity)

Scope decision

- **Flat table, not a master-detail document** — a deliberate structural departure from every prior Inventory module in this sub-sequence (Stock Entry/Opening Stock/Stock Adjustment/Stock Transfer/Stock Count are all header+items documents). A batch is inherently a single fact — "this lot of this product, in this warehouse, has this quantity, expiring on this date" — not a document composed of multiple line items. Modeled on `ProductPrice`'s flat per-product-per-tier shape instead (simple CRUD, two-FK composite uniqueness), the closest existing precedent for "one row scoped by two relations."
- **Composite uniqueness scoped to `(product_id, warehouse_id, batch_number)`**, not just `batch_number` alone — the same physical batch number could legitimately exist for two different products (manufacturer-assigned lot codes aren't globally unique across every product ever sold), and Stock Transfer could split one batch's quantity across two warehouses, so uniqueness needed to allow the same batch number to recur across products/warehouses while still preventing an accidental duplicate row for the exact same product+warehouse+batch combination. Verified in testing: the same `batch_number` was successfully created for the same product in a *different* warehouse, and correctly rejected when repeated in the *same* warehouse.
- `unit_cost` is nullable (matching Stock Entry's precedent, not Opening Stock's required precedent) — a batch record can exist before its cost is finalized.
- Added a `scopeExpired()` alongside the usual `scopeActive()` — a small, genuinely useful query helper for a table whose defining feature is an expiry date, and the first `scopeExpired`-style helper in this project. The index view's `expiry_date_formatted` column also visually flags a past-due batch with a red "Expired" badge inline, computed via `$row->expiry_date->isPast()` at render time (not stored) — the first "computed-and-badged, not stored" flag of this kind in this project, distinct from every prior module's `*_status` enum badges which read a stored column.

### 2026-08-03 (9)

Completed

- Serial Number Management (ninth Inventory module — tracks individual serialized units of a product, distinct from Batch Management's lot-quantity tracking)

Scope decision

- Same flat-table shape as `ProductBatch` (not a master-detail document) — a serial number, like a batch, is a single fact per row, not a document composed of line items. Reused `ProductBatch`'s exact CRUD/service/controller/request structure, adapted for this table's own columns.
- **Composite uniqueness scoped to `(product_id, serial_number)`, not `(product_id, warehouse_id, serial_number)`** like `ProductBatch` — a deliberate, documented difference between the two "sameish" modules. A batch's quantity can legitimately be split across multiple warehouses (the same lot, partially in two locations), so `ProductBatch` needed the warehouse in its uniqueness scope. A serial number identifies exactly **one physical unit**, which can only ever be in one place at a time — scoping uniqueness by warehouse as well would have allowed the same physical unit to be recorded as existing in two warehouses simultaneously, which is never valid. Verified in testing: the same `serial_number` was successfully created under a *different* product (manufacturer serial schemes aren't unique across every product ever made), and correctly rejected when repeated for the *same* product.
- **`warehouse_id` is nullable, `nullOnDelete`** (not `cascadeOnDelete` like `ProductBatch.warehouse_id`) — another deliberate, documented difference. A serialized unit's identity and history don't depend on which warehouse currently holds it; once sold, it may have no warehouse at all. Deleting a warehouse should not destroy the serial record of a unit that happens to currently be (or was) stored there — verified in testing that the serial survives with `warehouse_id` set to `null`, unlike a `ProductBatch` row, which is deliberately tied to its warehouse's lifecycle since a batch's quantity has no meaning independent of where it physically sits.
- **New `serial_status` enum (`in_stock`/`sold`/`defective`/`returned`)** — a genuinely richer per-unit lifecycle than `ProductBatch`'s plain active/inactive `status` toggle, since tracking an individual serialized unit's real-world state (on the shelf, sold to a customer, found defective, returned) is the entire point of serializing it in the first place; a batch, by contrast, doesn't need this since it's just a quantity, not a trackable individual item.

### 2026-08-03 (10)

Completed

- Inventory Transactions (tenth Inventory module — the unified, read-only stock movement ledger and live stock balance every prior Inventory module's changelog entry explicitly deferred to this module)

Scope decision

- **No new input table, no Model, no Service, no Form Request** — every prior Inventory module (Stock Entry, Opening Stock, Stock Adjustment, Stock Transfer) already captures the actual physical movement; building a fifth "manual transaction" table would duplicate that data entry and create two competing sources of truth. Instead, this module is a pure read-only aggregator, structurally the same "controller only, no CRUD layer" shape as every report page in this project (`SalesReportController`/`ProductReportController`/`PurchaseReportController`), just reading from four Inventory tables instead of one module's own table.
- **Computes a live stock balance from first principles, not from a stored running-total column** — `InventoryTransactionController::buildCurrentStockBalance()` sums every signed movement across all four source tables, grouped by `(product_id, warehouse_id)`, every time the page loads. This is the same "derive, never persist a figure that can drift out of sync" philosophy already used for `SalesInvoice::balance_due`/`PurchaseInvoice::balance_due`/`StockCountItem::variance`, just applied at a whole-ledger scale instead of a single record.
- **Signed-quantity merge across four structurally different sources**: Opening Stock and Stock Entry items are always positive (stock in); Stock Adjustment items are positive or negative depending on their own `adjustment_type` (`increase`/`decrease`); Stock Transfer items produce **two** ledger rows per line item — a negative "Stock Transfer (Out)" entry against the source warehouse and a positive "Stock Transfer (In)" entry against the destination warehouse — since a transfer is simultaneously a stock-out event for one warehouse and a stock-in event for another. This dual-row expansion for one source item is a new merge pattern for this project, not seen in any prior report controller (which always aggregate one row per source item).
- **Cancelled documents are excluded from the ledger** at the query level (`whereHas(..., fn ($q) => $q->where('*_status', '!=', 'cancelled'))` on each of the four source tables) — a cancelled Stock Entry/Adjustment/Transfer/Opening Stock never actually happened to real stock, so including it would corrupt the computed balance. This is the first place in this project where a report explicitly filters out a status value rather than just breaking a metric down *by* status.
- Both the current-balance table and the raw transaction history support the same `product_id`/`warehouse_id` GET-parameter filters, applied identically inside the one shared `buildTransactionLog()` method both the balance and history builds are derived from — filtering the underlying ledger once, not filtering two separately-computed datasets that could otherwise drift apart.

Database

- **No new tables** — reads across `opening_stock_items` (+ `opening_stocks`), `stock_entry_items` (+ `stock_entries`), `stock_adjustment_items` (+ `stock_adjustments`), and `stock_transfer_items` (+ `stock_transfers`), all already built in prior sessions this same day.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\InventoryTransactionController` — `index()` reads `product_id`/`warehouse_id` from the request, builds the merged/signed transaction log via `buildTransactionLog()` (described above), computes `totalIn`/`totalOut`/`netMovement` stat-tile figures directly from that log's signed quantities, calls `buildCurrentStockBalance()` (also described above) for the per-product/warehouse balance table, and derives `totalProductsTracked`/`totalWarehousesTracked`/`zeroOrNegativeCount` from that balance collection. Loads active `Product`/`Warehouse` lists for the two filter dropdowns.

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/inventory-transactions/index.blade.php` — a **new full-page (non-modal) view**, structurally similar to every prior report page in this project (`.stats-grid`/`.stat-card` tiles — 6 here) but with two new elements not seen in any prior report: **(1)** a plain `<form method="GET">` product/warehouse filter pair that submits on `change` (`onchange="this.form.submit()"`) rather than DataTables' AJAX-filter convention, since this page has no DataTable — it's two plain Blade `@forelse` tables (Current Stock Balance, Transaction History), not a paginated server-side grid, matching the same "plain table, not DataTables" precedent `CrmReportController`'s breakdown tables already established; **(2)** a "Clear Filters" link shown only when a filter is active, linking back to the unfiltered index route. Balance and quantity cells are conditionally red (`text-danger`) when a balance is zero/negative or a transaction is a stock-out, giving an at-a-glance visual read of the ledger without needing a chart.

Routes

- Added `GET admin/inventory-transactions` (`admin.inventory-transactions.index`) — a single route, no resource block, matching every other report page's shape exactly.

Permissions

- Added a single `inventory-transaction.view` (no create/edit/delete — a read-only ledger, same precedent as every other `*-report.view`-style permission in this project) to `database/seeders/RolePermissionSeeder.php` under the existing "Inventory" comment block, directly after `product-serial.*`. Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker.

- Extended `database/seeders/InventoryMenuSeeder.php` (existing file, not duplicated) with a new **top-level direct link** "Inventory Transactions" → `admin.inventory-transactions.index` at `order = 6` (below "Warehouses" through "Stock Count" at orders 0-5) — a primary page a user visits directly and often (the live stock ledger) gets a top-level link, same reasoning as every prior primary-entity module in this project, even though this one has no create/edit actions of its own. The "Inventory Masters" group's `order` was bumped from `6` to `7` to keep sibling `order` values unique among the module's `parent_id = null` rows, same order-collision-avoidance fix applied repeatedly throughout this project. ### 2026-08-03 (11)

Completed

- Stock Valuation (eleventh Inventory module — values current on-hand stock at each product's weighted-average unit cost)

Scope decision

- Same "controller-only, no new table/Model/Service" shape as Inventory Transactions — this is a report layered on top of data already captured by Opening Stock/Stock Entry/Stock Adjustment/Stock Transfer, not a new data-entry surface.
- **No stored "average cost" column anywhere** — `StockValuationController::buildWeightedAverageCosts()` derives a weighted-average unit cost per product fresh on every page load: `sum(quantity × unit_cost) ÷ sum(quantity)` across every cost-bearing Opening Stock and Stock Entry line for that product (across all warehouses combined, since cost is a property of the product's acquisition history, not tied to one location). Lines with a `null` unit_cost are **excluded from the average entirely**, not treated as a zero cost that would incorrectly drag the average down — verified in testing with a two-line weighted average (100 units @ 10 + 50 units @ 16 → exactly 12.00, not a naive unweighted average of 13).
- **Reuses the same current-balance computation as Inventory Transactions** (signed movements across all four source tables, cancelled documents excluded) but as its own self-contained private method rather than extracting a shared service — consistent with this project's existing precedent of each report controller computing its own aggregations independently (no cross-report service layer exists anywhere in this project, e.g. `SalesReportController`/`PurchaseReportController`/`ProductReportController` each have their own independent aggregation logic despite reading overlapping data). Extracting a shared `StockBalanceService` was considered but rejected as an unnecessary refactor of the just-shipped, already-verified `InventoryTransactionController` — out of scope for this task per the "don't modify existing modules unless required" rule.
- **Only positive on-hand balances are valued** — a zero or negative balance has no meaningful inventory value to report, so `buildCurrentStockBalance()` filters those out before the valuation step (a small, deliberate divergence from Inventory Transactions' own balance table, which intentionally *does* show zero/negative balances as a discrepancy signal — two different reports with two different reasons to include or exclude the same edge case).
- A product with an on-hand balance but **no recorded cost anywhere** is shown with `total_value = null` and a "No cost data" label rather than silently valuing it at zero — a zero value would misrepresent real stock as worthless; `null` correctly signals "unknown," and the `productsWithNoCostData` stat tile surfaces exactly how many such lines exist so an admin knows to go back and record costs.

Database

### 2026-08-03 (12)

Completed

- Reorder Level (twelfth Inventory module — a per-product, optionally per-warehouse, minimum-stock-threshold setting; the input data the next module, Low Stock Alerts, will read against the live stock balance already computed by Inventory Transactions/Stock Valuation)

Scope decision

- Inspected `Product`, `Warehouse`, `ProductBatch`/`ProductBatchController` (closest existing flat-lookup precedent with two FK filters), and `InventoryTransactionController`/`StockValuationController`'s balance-computation logic directly before starting. Reorder Level is deliberately a **flat setting table, not a master-detail document** — same structural family as `ProductBatch`/`ProductSerial`, not the header+items movement documents (Stock Entry/Opening Stock/Stock Adjustment/Stock Transfer/Stock Count).
- **`warehouse_id` is nullable, `nullOnDelete`** — a `null` warehouse means "this reorder level applies across all warehouses for this product," while a specific warehouse row overrides that global setting for just that location. This mirrors `Price Lists`' `customer_group_id` nullable-means-broader-scope convention from Sales, applied here to the product/warehouse dimension instead. `product_id` is required, `cascadeOnDelete` — a reorder level has no meaning without the product it thresholds, same reasoning as every required parent-owns-child FK in this project.
- **Composite unique index `(product_id, warehouse_id)`** was added at the schema level, but — documented explicitly since it's a real, verified limitation — MySQL's unique index treats multiple `NULL` values in `warehouse_id` as distinct, so it does **not** by itself block two different "global" (warehouse-blank) reorder levels for the same product. The DB index still correctly blocks a duplicate *specific*-warehouse row (verified in testing). The global-row case is guarded at the **Form Request level only**, via a `Rule::unique('reorder_levels','warehouse_id')->where(...)` closure that branches on whether `warehouse_id` was submitted: if set, it scopes to that exact warehouse (redundant with, but consistent with, the DB constraint); if blank, it scopes via `whereNull('warehouse_id')` instead — the same "DB unique index handles the has-a-value case; the Form Request additionally handles the both-null case" split already required by every nullable-FK composite-unique table in this project's history (though this is the first one where the *app-level* rule is strictly necessary rather than just a friendlier error message, since the DB index genuinely cannot enforce the null case on its own).
- No `reorder_quantity` enforcement (`nullable`) — a business may set a threshold without yet deciding how much to reorder each time; the future Low Stock Alerts module can fall back to some other default when it's absent, out of scope for this task.
- No relation was added on `Product`/`Warehouse` (e.g. `reorderLevels(): HasMany`) — same "avoid speculative relations" reasoning used throughout this project; trivial to add later if a future view needs it.

Database

- Added `reorder_levels` migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_03_180000_create_reorder_levels_table.php`): `product_id` required `foreignId` → `products.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `warehouse_id` nullable `foreignId` → `warehouses.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `reorder_level` decimal(15,2) default 0 (the minimum threshold); `reorder_quantity` decimal(15,2) nullable (the suggested amount to reorder); `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean default true; named composite unique index `rl_product_warehouse_unique` on `(product_id, warehouse_id)` (custom short index name, same MySQL-identifier-length reasoning as every other multi-column named unique index in this project, e.g. `pv_av_unique`/`pb_product_warehouse_batch_unique`).

Models

- Added `App\Models\ReorderLevel` — fillable `product_id, warehouse_id, reorder_level, reorder_quantity, notes, status`; casts `status` boolean, `reorder_level`/`reorder_quantity` to `decimal:2`; relations `product()`, `warehouse()` (both `BelongsTo`); `scopeActive()`.

Services

- Added `App\Services\ReorderLevelService` — plain `create()`/`update()`/`delete()`, same minimal shape as `ProductBatchService`/`ProductSerialService`.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\ReorderLevelRequest` — `product_id` required `exists:products,id`; `warehouse_id` nullable `exists:warehouses,id` plus the branching `Rule::unique('reorder_levels','warehouse_id')->where(...)->ignore($id)` closure described in the Scope decision above (ignore resolved via `$this->route('reorder_level')?->id`, same route-model-binding technique used throughout this project's edit-aware unique rules); `reorder_level` required numeric `min:0`; `reorder_quantity` nullable numeric `min:0`; `notes`/`status` standard. Custom message for the unique rule clarifying both the specific-warehouse and "All Warehouses" cases.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\ReorderLevelController` — mirrors `ProductBatchController`'s two-FK-dropdown shape: index eager-loads `product`/`warehouse`, adds `product_id`/`warehouse_id` AJAX filters beyond the standard `status`/`search`, search matches the parent product's `name`/`sku` via `whereHas`. DataTable's `warehouse_name` column shows "All Warehouses" (not a blank/dash) when `warehouse_id` is null — the same "meaningful label for the null case" idiom `DeliveryController`'s "Walk-in Customer" label and `Delivery`'s no-vendor-column precedent already established, here signaling that the setting is global rather than empty/unset. `create()`/`edit()` load active `Product`/`Warehouse` lists for the two relation dropdowns.

Views

### 2026-08-03 (13)

Completed

- Low Stock Alerts (thirteenth Inventory module — a read-only report comparing each product/warehouse's live stock balance against the threshold set in Reorder Level, surfacing everything that needs restocking)

Scope decision

- Inspected `InventoryTransactionController`/`StockValuationController` directly before starting, and `ReorderLevel` (built in the prior session) for its global-vs-specific scoping shape. Same "controller-only, no new table/Model/Service/Request" pattern as those two prior reports — this module introduces zero new input, it just cross-references stock the balance-computation logic already derives against the threshold data Reorder Level already stores.
- **Reuses the exact signed-movement balance aggregation** (`buildCurrentStockBalance()`) from `InventoryTransactionController`/`StockValuationController` as its own self-contained copy, per this project's established precedent that each report controller computes its own aggregations independently rather than sharing a service (documented explicitly in Stock Valuation's own changelog entry, and followed here rather than retroactively extracting a shared service — out of scope, would require touching two already-shipped, already-verified controllers). One deliberate divergence from Stock Valuation's copy: **zero/negative balances are kept, not filtered out** — Stock Valuation excludes them because a non-positive balance has no meaningful *value* to report, but a non-positive (or below-threshold) balance is exactly what this report exists to surface, so filtering it out here would defeat the module's purpose.
- **New reorder-level-resolution logic, not present in any prior report**: `buildReorderLevels()` splits all active `ReorderLevel` rows into two lookup maps — one keyed by the exact `"product_id|warehouse_id"` pair (a warehouse-specific threshold) and one keyed by just `product_id` (a `warehouse_id = null` row, applying globally) — then for each balance row, a specific-warehouse threshold is checked first and a global one is used as the fallback, exactly matching the precedence `ReorderLevel`'s own changelog entry described ("a specific-warehouse row overrides that global setting for just that location"). A balance row with **no** matching threshold at all (neither specific nor global) is excluded entirely — there is nothing to compare it against, so it cannot be "low" or "not low," it's simply untracked for this purpose.
- **Known, documented scope limitation** (same category as Product Images' orphaned-file note / Product Bundles' cascade-emptied-bundle note elsewhere in this project): a product/warehouse combination only appears in this report if it has **some** recorded movement history (an Opening Stock/Stock Entry/Stock Adjustment/Stock Transfer line) — a brand-new product with a Reorder Level configured but zero actual stock movements ever recorded for a given warehouse will not appear as an alert, even though its real-world balance is effectively zero there. This is the same limitation already implicit in `buildCurrentStockBalance()`'s design (it can only report on combinations that exist in the transaction log), inherited here rather than newly introduced; flagged explicitly since it's the first place a Reorder Level threshold could silently fail to trigger an alert for exactly this reason.
- Alerts are sorted by largest shortfall (`reorder_level - balance`) first — the most urgent restocking need surfaces at the top, distinct from Inventory Transactions' chronological ordering and Stock Valuation's highest-value-first ordering.

Database

- **No new tables** — reads the same four movement tables (`opening_stock_items`/`opening_stocks`, `stock_entry_items`/`stock_entries`, `stock_adjustment_items`/`stock_adjustments`, `stock_transfer_items`/`stock_transfers`) Inventory Transactions/Stock Valuation already read, plus the `reorder_levels` table built in the prior session.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\LowStockAlertController` — `index()` reads `product_id`/`warehouse_id` filters, builds the current balance via its own `buildCurrentStockBalance()` (described above, balances kept including zero/negative), resolves each row's applicable threshold via `buildReorderLevels()`, filters to rows where `balance <= reorder_level`, computes `shortfall` per row, sorts by shortfall descending, and derives `totalAlerts`/`productsAffected`/`warehousesAffected`/`totalShortfallQuantity`/`outOfStockCount` (rows with `balance <= 0`) stat-tile figures from that filtered collection. Loads active `Product`/`Warehouse` lists for the two filter dropdowns.

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/low-stock-alerts/index.blade.php` — a **new full-page (non-modal) view**, structurally matching Stock Valuation's/Inventory Transactions' report shape (`.stats-grid` tiles — 5 here; plain `GET`-form product/warehouse filters submitting on `change`; a "Clear Filters" link shown only when a filter is active; a single plain `@forelse` table, no DataTables). The balance and shortfall cells are conditionally red (`text-danger`) — the balance cell only when it's zero/negative (an out-of-stock, not merely low-stock, condition), the shortfall cell always (since every row in this table is by definition a shortfall) — same "conditionally-colored cell for an at-a-glance read" idiom Inventory Transactions' own view already established. "Suggested Reorder Qty" shows `-` when the underlying `ReorderLevel.reorder_quantity` was left blank, matching that field's own documented optionality.

Routes

- Added `GET admin/low-stock-alerts` (`admin.low-stock-alerts.index`) — a single route, no resource block, matching every other report page's shape exactly (`inventory-transactions`, `stock-valuation`, and every `*-report`/`*-forecast`/`*-dashboard` page in this project).

Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker.

- Chart of Accounts (first Accounting module — a self-referencing tree of financial accounts classified by fixed accounting type, the foundational entity every later Accounting sub-module — Journal Entries, General Ledger, Trial Balance, etc. — will post against)

Scope decision

- Checked the Naming/Table Conflict Guard first — no `chart_of_accounts`-named table existed anywhere; no collision. Accounting is a brand-new top-level module (previously HRM, Workflow Engine, CRM, Product Management, Sales, Purchase, and Inventory existed), following the exact same `Module`/`ModuleMenu` seeder pattern as every prior new module.
- **Built as a self-referencing tree, reusing the Categories tree-redesign pattern exactly** (`parent_id` nullable self-ref, `nullOnDelete`, `descendantIds()`/`indentedOptions()` helpers, cycle-prevention via `Rule::notIn` + a `withValidator()` closure, a recursive `_node.blade.php` partial, plain-jQuery expand/collapse/search JS with no new dependency) — a chart of accounts is inherently hierarchical (Assets → Current Assets → Cash in Hand) in every real accounting system, the same structural shape Categories already solved for Product Management.
- **`account_type` is a fixed 5-value enum (`asset`/`liability`/`equity`/`revenue`/`expense`), not a separate lookup table** — even though erp.txt lists "Account Types" as its own next roadmap checklist item. This mirrors the exact ordering situation already resolved for Products/Product Variants: erp.txt's literal order doesn't reflect a hard technical dependency here, since the 5 fundamental account types are a fixed, universal accounting classification that never varies per-business (unlike, say, Product Categories). Every account needs this classification from day one to be usable at all, so it's implemented now as a `Rule::in()`-validated enum (`ChartOfAccount::ACCOUNT_TYPES`), the same "hardcoded enum now, retrofit an FK later only if a real need appears" choice already made for Categories' pre-tree flat shape and Sales Quotations' status lifecycle. If the upcoming "Account Types" module turns out to need finer-grained sub-classification (e.g. QuickBooks-style "Current Asset"/"Fixed Asset"/"Bank" sub-types), an optional `account_type_id` FK can be retrofitted onto this table later via the "build the dependency, then retrofit" pattern already used repeatedly (Customer Groups → `customers.customer_group_id`, Departments → `designations.department_id`) — not built speculatively here.
- **`normal_balance` (debit or credit) is a computed accessor, not a stored column** — asset/expense accounts always increase with a debit and liability/equity/revenue accounts always increase with a credit; this is a fixed rule of double-entry accounting derived entirely from `account_type`, so storing it as an independent column would just create a second value that could drift out of sync with the account's own type. Same "derive, never persist a derivable figure" philosophy as `SalesInvoice::balance_due`/`StockCountItem::variance`/`Inventory Transactions`' live balance.
- **`is_group` (boolean) marks header/organizational accounts** (e.g. "Assets", "Current Assets") versus postable leaf accounts (e.g. "Cash in Hand") — a standard, universal accounting-software concept (QuickBooks/Xero/Tally all distinguish header accounts from detail accounts) added now rather than retrofitted later, since the upcoming Journal Entries module will need to know which accounts are valid posting targets and which are purely structural; not enforced at the DB/service level in this task (no journal-posting logic exists yet to enforce against), just captured as data for that future module to read.
- **`code` is globally unique** (not scoped per-parent the way Categories' `name` is) — real-world chart-of-accounts numbering conventions (e.g. "1000", "1010", "2000") are unique across the entire chart, not just within a sibling group, so the uniqueness rule is a plain global `Rule::unique()` rather than a `where('parent_id', ...)`-scoped one.

Database

- Added `chart_of_accounts` migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_04_090000_create_chart_of_accounts_table.php`): `parent_id` nullable `foreignId` → `chart_of_accounts.id` (self-referencing), `nullOnDelete` — deleting a parent promotes its children to top-level rather than deleting the whole subtree, same choice already verified for Categories; `code` unique required string; `name` required string; `account_type` enum (`asset`/`liability`/`equity`/`revenue`/`expense`), no default (always required); `is_group` boolean default false; `description` nullable text; `status` boolean default true.

Models

- Added `App\Models\ChartOfAccount` — `protected $table = 'chart_of_accounts'` (explicit, since Eloquent's default pluralization of `ChartOfAccount` would resolve to `chart_of_accounts` correctly anyway, but made explicit for clarity given the unusual multi-word model name); fillable `parent_id, code, name, account_type, is_group, description, status`; `public const ACCOUNT_TYPES` and `public const NORMAL_BALANCE_MAP` (single source of truth for the Form Request's `Rule::in()` and the `normal_balance` accessor respectively); casts `is_group`/`status` to boolean; relations `parent()`/`children()` (self-referencing `BelongsTo`/`HasMany` via `parent_id`, same pattern as `Category`); `getNormalBalanceAttribute()`; `scopeActive()`; `descendantIds()` and `indentedOptions()` (both copied from `Category`'s exact implementation, the latter formatted as "`code` - `name`" per option rather than just `name`, since an accountant navigating a COA dropdown needs the code visible to disambiguate similarly-named accounts).

Services

- Added `App\Services\ChartOfAccountService` — plain `create()`/`update()`/`delete()`, same minimal shape as `CategoryService`.

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\ChartOfAccountRequest` — `parent_id` nullable `exists:chart_of_accounts,id` plus `Rule::notIn([$id])` on edit (an account can't be its own parent); `code` required unique globally (`Rule::unique('chart_of_accounts','code')->ignore($id)`); `name` required; `account_type` required `Rule::in(ChartOfAccount::ACCOUNT_TYPES)`; `is_group` required boolean; `description`/`status` standard. A `withValidator()` closure (copied from `CategoryRequest`'s exact pattern) rejects the update if the chosen `parent_id` is one of the account's own descendants, preventing a cycle.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\ChartOfAccountController` — exact structural mirror of `CategoryController`: `index()` loads the full ordered-by-code collection once and hands it to the recursive tree partial (no DataTables AJAX endpoint, acceptable query cost for admin-only master data, same assumption already made for Categories); `create()` accepts `?parent_id=` for the tree's per-node "Add Sub-account" button; `edit()` excludes the account itself and all its descendants from the parent dropdown (defense-in-depth alongside the Form Request's cycle check, same as Categories). Uses `ActivityLogger`, module string `chart-of-accounts`.

Views

- No `action.blade.php` was created — same as Categories, per-row actions (Add Sub-account/Edit/Delete) render directly inside `_node.blade.php`, so there's no separate DataTable row-action partial to generate.

Routes

Route-model-binding param is `{chart_of_account}`.

Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto the existing "Super Admin" role via tinker per established precedent (seeder still not idempotent, not re-run wholesale).

### 2026-08-04 (2)

Completed

- Account Types (second Accounting module — a flat lookup of finer-grained account sub-classifications, e.g. "Bank"/"Fixed Asset"/"Current Liability", each tagged with one of the 5 fixed accounting natures) plus a follow-up migration retrofitting an optional `account_type_id` onto the already-shipped `chart_of_accounts` table

Scope decision

- This closes the gap flagged explicitly in Chart of Accounts' own changelog entry: `account_type` there is a fixed, universal 5-value enum (asset/liability/equity/revenue/expense) that drives `normal_balance` and can never be reclassified; "Account Types" is the finer, admin-configurable sub-classification layered on top of it (the QuickBooks/Xero-style "detail type" concept — e.g. multiple sub-types like "Bank" and "Cash" both share the `asset` nature but are meaningfully distinct for reporting/UX purposes). Followed the exact "build the dependency, then retrofit the FK" pattern already used repeatedly in this project (Customer Groups → `customers.customer_group_id`, Departments → `designations.department_id`, Sales Targets → `sales_orders.assigned_to`).
- **Flat lookup table, not a tree** — unlike Chart of Accounts itself, account sub-types (Bank, Cash, Accounts Receivable, Fixed Asset, ...) are conceptually siblings under a fixed nature, not a hierarchy; this is a simple `name`/`nature`/`description`/`status` CRUD module, the same shape as `Brand`/`Unit`/`PriceTier` rather than another self-referencing tree.
- **`nature` is required and reuses the exact same 5-value set as `ChartOfAccount::ACCOUNT_TYPES`** — defined as its own `AccountType::NATURES` constant (per this project's established "each model owns its own enum constant even when the value set is conceptually shared" convention, e.g. `SalesOrder::STATUSES` vs `SalesQuotation::STATUSES` both being independently-defined 5-ish-value sets) rather than importing `ChartOfAccount`'s constant directly, avoiding a cross-model coupling for what is otherwise just a shared vocabulary.
- **Retrofit adds `chart_of_accounts.account_type_id` as nullable, `nullOnDelete`, alongside the existing required `account_type` enum column — not a replacement for it.** An account can optionally carry a specific sub-type (e.g. "Bank") in addition to its mandatory fixed nature (`asset`); if the assigned Account Type is later deleted, the Chart of Accounts entry survives with `account_type_id` cleared, but its `account_type`/`normal_balance` are completely unaffected, since those are derived from the separate, always-present enum column, never from this optional FK.
- **New cross-field validation, not present in any prior "optional classification" retrofit in this project**: `ChartOfAccountRequest` now has a second `withValidator()` closure verifying that if `account_type_id` is set, the chosen `AccountType`'s own `nature` matches the Chart of Accounts entry's `account_type` — rejecting, for example, assigning a `liability`-natured sub-type ("Current Liability") to an `asset`-natured account. This is a genuinely new validation pattern for this project (a cross-table nature-consistency check, not just a uniqueness/cycle check like every prior `withValidator()` closure), verified directly in testing (a `liability`-natured Account Type correctly detected as a mismatch against an `asset` Chart of Accounts entry).

Database

- Added `account_types` migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_04_100000_create_account_types_table.php`): `name` unique required, `nature` enum (`asset`/`liability`/`equity`/`revenue`/`expense`, no default — always required), `description` nullable text, `status` boolean default true. Identical flat shape to every simple lookup module in this project.
- Added a follow-up migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_04_100001_add_account_type_id_to_chart_of_accounts_table.php`, not an edit to the original Chart of Accounts migration) adding `account_type_id` nullable `foreignId` → `account_types.id`, `nullOnDelete`, positioned `->after('account_type')`.

- Updated `App\Models\ChartOfAccount` — added `account_type_id` to `$fillable`, added `accountType(): BelongsTo` (→ `AccountType` via `account_type_id`, non-default relation name since the FK column name overlaps conceptually — but not literally — with the existing `account_type` enum column).

- Updated `App\Http\Requests\Admin\ChartOfAccountRequest` — added `account_type_id` nullable `exists:account_types,id`; added a second `withValidator()` closure (described in the Scope decision above) that loads the selected `AccountType` and compares its `nature` against the submitted `account_type`, adding a friendly, specific error message (naming both the mismatched values) rather than a generic validation failure when they disagree.

Controllers

Rendered `account-types.index()`/`.create()` and `chart-of-accounts.index()`/`.create()` all four directly, confirming no fatal Blade errors on any of them (only the same known unauthenticated-topbar warnings seen in every prior tinker-rendered-view test in this project). ### 2026-08-04 (3)

Completed

- Journal Entries (third Accounting module — the manual double-entry posting mechanism every later Accounting sub-module, General Ledger through Financial Reports, will read from; the first genuinely new master-detail shape in Accounting)

Scope decision

- Inspected `SalesQuotation`/`SalesQuotationService`/`SalesQuotationController` (the closest existing "header + priced line items, live totals preview" precedent) and `ChartOfAccount`'s own footer note ("journal entries can only be posted to non-group accounts") directly before starting. Reused the exact delete-then-recreate `syncItems()`/`calculateTotals()` service shape and the `'xl'`-modal repeatable-row builder pattern, but this module's defining feature — and the reason it's more than a copy-paste of Sales Quotations — is the **double-entry balance rule**, a genuinely new class of cross-line validation for this project.
- **`journal_entry_items` (not "lines")** — kept the project's established `_items` naming convention (`sales_order_items`, `product_bundle_items`, etc.) rather than switching to accounting-conventional "lines" terminology at the table/model level; the create/edit UI labels them "Journal Lines" for the user-facing accounting vocabulary, but the underlying table/model/relation names stay consistent with every other master-detail module in this codebase.
- **New Form Request validation pattern — a real double-entry balance check, not just a uniqueness/cycle check like every prior `withValidator()` closure in this project**: `JournalEntryRequest::withValidator()` enforces three rules simultaneously, none of which existed anywhere in this codebase before: **(1)** each line must be *either* a debit *or* a credit, never both and never neither (`($debit > 0 && $credit > 0) || ($debit <= 0 && $credit <= 0)` is rejected); **(2)** `sum(debit)` must exactly equal `sum(credit)` across all lines (`round(...,2) !== round(...,2)`, avoiding float-equality pitfalls) — the fundamental rule of double-entry bookkeeping; **(3)** no line may post to a group/header `ChartOfAccount` (`is_group = true`), enforced here in code for the first time despite being flagged as a future requirement in Chart of Accounts' own footer note two sessions ago. `items` also requires `min:2` (a balanced entry needs at least one debit line and one credit line).
- **`chart_of_account_id` is required, `cascadeOnDelete`** — matching the same "required parent-owns-child FK, `cascadeOnDelete`, documented as an accepted data-integrity tradeoff" precedent already used for every product-line-item FK in this project (e.g. `sales_order_items.product_id`), rather than introducing this project's first `restrictOnDelete()`. This is a deliberate, explicit choice: deleting a `ChartOfAccount` that has historical journal postings will silently cascade-delete those line items (potentially leaving the parent `JournalEntry`'s stored `total_debit`/`total_credit` out of sync with its now-smaller set of surviving lines) — verified directly in testing. This is the same category of accepted gap already flagged for Product Bundles ("cascade-emptied bundles") and Product Images ("orphaned files"), not a new kind of risk introduced by this module; a real double-entry ERP would eventually need to prevent deleting an account with posting history (a `restrictOnDelete`-style guard), but that's a bigger design decision (this project has never used `restrictOnDelete()` anywhere) intentionally left as a documented follow-up rather than introduced ad hoc in this task.
- **`entry_status` reuses the exact 3-value shape** (`draft`/`posted`/`cancelled`) already established by Stock Entry/Opening Stock/Stock Adjustment in Inventory — the same "recorded but not yet finalized vs. finalized vs. voided" document lifecycle, just applied to a financial posting instead of a stock movement. `created_by` is auto-set server-side from the authenticated admin (never client-submitted), same pattern as `RelationshipHistory.created_by`/`EmailCommunication.created_by`.
- **New client-side UX not present in any prior item-row JS in this project**: entering a value in a line's Debit field automatically clears that same line's Credit field (and vice versa), directly encoding rule (1) above as an interactive guardrail rather than only a server-side rejection; and a live "Balanced"/"Out of balance"/"Add lines" badge (green/red/grey) updates in real time as lines are added, removed, or edited — a genuinely new "pass/fail indicator badge" UI element, distinct from every prior item-row JS's plain numeric totals preview (Sales Quotations/Orders/Invoices/Credit Notes/Supplier Quotations/Purchase Orders/Purchase Invoices/Debit Notes all show a running total, none of them show a computed correctness verdict).

Database

- Added `journal_entries`/`journal_entry_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_04_110000_create_journal_entries_table.php`):
  - `journal_entries`: `entry_number` unique (server-generated); `entry_date` required date; `reference` nullable string (an external document/invoice reference, free-text); `narration` nullable text; `total_debit`/`total_credit` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only (never client-submitted, same convention as every Sales/Purchase financial document's totals); `entry_status` enum (`draft`/`posted`/`cancelled`) default `draft`; `created_by` nullable `foreignId` → `admins.id`, `nullOnDelete`; `status` boolean.
  - `journal_entry_items`: `journal_entry_id` `cascadeOnDelete`; `chart_of_account_id` required `foreignId` → `chart_of_accounts.id`, `cascadeOnDelete` (per the Scope decision above); `debit`/`credit` decimal(15,2) default 0 (both present on every line — exactly one is expected to be non-zero, enforced at the Form Request level, not a DB `CHECK` constraint, consistent with this project's "business rules live in the Form Request, not the schema" convention already stated for `workflow_steps`' dual-parent FK); `description` nullable string (a per-line memo). No unique constraint on `(journal_entry_id, chart_of_account_id)` — the same account can legitimately appear on multiple lines of a compound entry (e.g. splitting one payment across two expense sub-accounts).

Models

- Added `App\Models\JournalEntry` — fillable `entry_number, entry_date, reference, narration, total_debit, total_credit, entry_status, created_by, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','posted','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `entry_date` to `date`, both totals to `decimal:2`; relations `createdBy()` (→ `Admin` via `created_by`, non-default relation name, same pattern as `PurchaseRequest::requestedBy()`), `items(): HasMany` (→ `JournalEntryItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\JournalEntryItem` — fillable `journal_entry_id, chart_of_account_id, debit, credit, description`; casts `debit`/`credit` to `decimal:2`; relations `journalEntry()`, `chartOfAccount()`.

Services

- Added `App\Services\JournalEntryService` — structural copy of `SalesQuotationService`: `generateEntryNumber()` (`'JE-' . str_pad(JournalEntry::max('id')+1, 6, '0', STR_PAD_LEFT)`, a new `JE-` prefix, distinct from every other document reference number in this project), `calculateTotals()` (sums `debit`/`credit` across submitted items into `total_debit`/`total_credit` — simpler than every prior `calculateTotals()` in this project, since there's no `quantity × unit_price` math here, just a straight sum of two pre-entered amounts), `syncItems()` (identical delete-then-recreate strategy).

Requests

The three-rule `withValidator()` closure described in the Scope decision above (debit-xor-credit per line, balanced totals, no posting to group accounts) is the module's core new logic.

### 2026-08-04 (4)

Completed

- General Ledger (fourth Accounting module — a pure read-only per-account running-balance report built entirely from posted Journal Entries, no new table/model/service)

Scope decision

- Same "controller only, no CRUD layer" pattern as Inventory Transactions/Stock Valuation. No new input — Journal Entries already captures every movement; this reads across `journal_entry_items`/`journal_entries` and layers a running balance on top, per-account.
- **Only `entry_status = 'posted'` journal entries are counted** — a deliberately *stricter* filter than every Inventory report's `!= 'cancelled'` convention (which still counts `draft`-equivalent documents as real). A journal entry's `draft` state means it hasn't been finalized as an accounting fact yet, so it has no place in a ledger balance the same way an unposted stock entry still represents "goods physically received" — verified directly in testing: a `draft` entry was correctly excluded from both the per-account detail and the summary.
- **Two-mode single page, not two separate screens**: with no `account_id` selected, the page shows a lightweight ending-balance-per-account **summary** (deliberately minimal — code/name/type/total debit/total credit/balance only, no percentage breakdowns or charts) so the page isn't empty on first load and so an admin can click into any account; selecting an account switches the same page to the full running-balance **detail** view. This mirrors the existing "`?employee_id=` toggles between full list and filtered view" convention used by HRM's employee-scoped child modules, adapted to a report instead of a CRUD list. The summary is kept intentionally shallow so it doesn't preempt the **Trial Balance** report (a later, separate roadmap item, whose entire job is a comprehensive all-accounts debit/credit table) — General Ledger's summary is a navigation aid to the per-account detail, not a competing "mini trial balance."
- **New computation not present in any prior Accounting/Inventory report**: a real **opening balance carried forward**. When `date_from` is supplied, everything posted *before* that date is summed into an `opening_balance` (not discarded/ignored the way a plain date-range filter would), and the running balance for the filtered lines continues from that figure rather than restarting at zero — verified directly in testing (an account showing a `1000` opening balance brought forward from an entry before the filter date, then correctly continuing to `700` after one more filtered-in transaction). This is the first "brought-forward" balance concept in this project; every prior date-filtered report (Sales/Purchase Reports, Inventory Transactions) just filters a window and reports on that window alone, with no notion of "what came before."
- **Signed balance direction depends on the account's `normal_balance` accessor** (already established by Chart of Accounts): for a debit-normal account (asset/expense), `running_balance += debit - credit`; for a credit-normal account (liability/equity/revenue), `running_balance += credit - debit`. Verified directly in testing with the same journal entries read through both a debit-normal account (Cash) and a credit-normal account (Revenue) — both correctly ended at the same magnitude (700) despite the opposite sign convention, exactly as double-entry bookkeeping requires (a debit to one side is always a credit to the other).
- Only **postable (non-group)** `ChartOfAccount`s are offered in the account filter dropdown — the same accounts Journal Entries already restricts postings to, since a group/header account can never have a journal line and therefore never has a ledger to show.

Database

- **No new tables** — reads `journal_entry_items`/`journal_entries` (built in the previous session) and `chart_of_accounts` (for the account list and each account's `normal_balance`). No Model, no Service, no Form Request, no CRUD routes.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\GeneralLedgerController` — `index()` reads `account_id`/`date_from`/`date_to`, loads active non-group `ChartOfAccount`s for the filter dropdown; when `account_id` is set, calls `buildAccountLedger()` (opening balance brought forward, per-line running balance, closing totals — described above); otherwise calls `buildAccountsSummary()` (ending balance per account as of `date_to`, or across all time if not given). A shared `signedSum()` helper centralizes the normal-balance-aware sign logic used by both methods, so the summary and detail views can never disagree about which direction a balance moves for a given account (verified directly in testing — the summary's Cash balance matched the detail view's closing balance exactly).

Views

- Added `resources/views/admin/general-ledger/index.blade.php` — a **new full-page (non-modal) report view**, following the plain `GET`-form filter + `@forelse` table shape every prior report page in this project uses, extended with a third filter (`account_id`, alongside `date_from`/`date_to` — the first Accounting/Inventory report to combine a relation filter with a date-range filter simultaneously) and a `@if($selectedAccount && $ledger) ... @else ... @endif` split rendering either the 4-stat-tile + running-balance detail table or the lightweight accounts-summary table, per the Scope decision above. The detail table's first row is always a highlighted "Opening Balance" line (not just a stat tile) so the running balance's starting point is visible directly in the transaction list, not only summarized above it.

Inserted live via `Permission::firstOrCreate(...)` and synced onto "Super Admin" via tinker.

### 2026-08-04 (5)

Completed

- Cash Book (fifth Accounting module — the same per-account running-balance mechanics as General Ledger, scoped to only Cash/Bank accounts and relabelled in cash-book terms: Receipts/Payments instead of Debit/Credit)

Scope decision

- Inspected `GeneralLedgerController` directly before starting. Cash Book is deliberately **not** a thin wrapper or subclass of it — it's a self-contained duplicate of the same balance-computation logic, per this project's established precedent (documented explicitly in Stock Valuation's, Low Stock Alerts', and General Ledger's own changelog entries) that each report controller computes its own aggregation independently rather than sharing a service, so that editing one report's logic later can never accidentally change another's behavior.
- **"Cash account" is identified by a label-matching heuristic, not a dedicated column**: a postable, `asset`-natured `ChartOfAccount` whose optional `accountType` (the sub-classification retrofitted onto Chart of Accounts two sessions ago) has a `name` containing "cash" or "bank" (case-insensitive `LIKE`). This is the same "match by label text" heuristic already used and documented as a known, accepted limitation elsewhere in this project (e.g. `CrmReportController`'s lead-conversion-rate metric matching on a status label) — verified directly in testing that this correctly includes an account tagged with an Account Type named "Cash Smoke" while correctly excluding a plain `asset` account with no Account Type assigned at all. If no admin has ever created and assigned a Cash/Bank-named Account Type, the page honestly shows nothing to select (with an explanatory message and direct links to both prerequisite screens) rather than guessing.
- **Every Cash Book account is asset-natured by construction** (enforced by the `account_type = 'asset'` filter), so unlike General Ledger's generic `normal_balance`-branching signed-sum logic, Cash Book's running balance is always simply `receipts (debit) − payments (credit)` — no branching needed, since a cash/bank account can never legitimately be liability/equity/revenue-natured.
- Same two-mode single-page shape as General Ledger (no account selected → a lightweight closing-balance-per-account summary; one selected → full running-balance detail), plus one new headline figure General Ledger's summary doesn't have: a **"Total Cash & Bank Balance"** stat tile (the sum of every cash/bank account's closing balance) — a genuinely useful "how much cash does the business have right now" figure that's specific to this scoped-down report and wouldn't make sense on General Ledger's all-accounts summary (summing balances across asset, liability, equity, and revenue accounts together would be meaningless).
- Reused the exact opening-balance-brought-forward mechanism General Ledger introduced last session (sum everything posted before `date_from`, continue the running balance from there rather than restarting at zero) — verified again here with a fresh test to confirm it holds for this scoped-down report too.

Database

- **No new tables** — reads the same `journal_entry_items`/`journal_entries`/`chart_of_accounts` (plus `account_types`, via the `ChartOfAccount::accountType()` relation) every other Accounting module already reads. No Model, no Service, no Form Request, no CRUD routes.

### 2026-08-04 (6)

Completed

- Bank Accounts (sixth Accounting module — company/business bank account master data, distinct from HRM's employee-scoped personal bank details)

Scope decision

- Checked the Naming/Table Conflict Guard first, exactly as it instructs: HRM already owns `bank_accounts` (Employee → BankAccount, personal salary bank details), so this module's table is `finance_bank_accounts`, per the Guard's own explicit instruction. Model is `App\Models\FinanceBankAccount` (matching the table name, not a bare `BankAccount` that would collide in spirit if not in fact with HRM's `BankAccount` model), routes/permissions/menu all prefixed `finance-bank-account(s)`.
- **Standard flat CRUD module** (like `Vendor`/`Warehouse`), not a master-detail document — a bank account is a single master record (bank name, account holder, account number, branch, IFSC/SWIFT, currency, opening balance), not a document composed of line items.
- **Optional `chart_of_account_id` link to Chart of Accounts** — a genuinely new connective feature: a bank account master record can (optionally) be tied to its corresponding GL account, so future modules (Bank Transactions, Bank Reconciliation) have a ready-made bridge between "the real-world bank account" and "the ledger account that represents it," without forcing every bank account to have one set up immediately. `nullOnDelete` — deleting the linked `ChartOfAccount` leaves the bank account record intact with the link cleared, same as every other optional FK in this project.
- **Reused Journal Entries' own "no posting to group accounts" validation pattern**: `FinanceBankAccountRequest`'s `withValidator()` rejects linking to a `ChartOfAccount` where `is_group = true`, since a bank account should map to a real, postable ledger account, not an organizational header — the same rule already enforced for journal entry lines, applied here to a different linking context.
- `account_number` is globally unique (a real bank account number shouldn't be registered twice as two separate master records). `currency` is a plain free-text field defaulting to `"USD"` in the form (no currency master/lookup table introduced — out of scope, proportionate to what erp.txt's "Bank Accounts" feature actually calls for).

### 2026-08-04 (7)

Completed

- Bank Transactions (seventh Accounting module — individual deposit/withdrawal records against a `FinanceBankAccount`, feeding the next roadmap item, Bank Reconciliation)

Scope decision

- **Flat CRUD, not a master-detail document** — a bank transaction is a single fact (one deposit or one withdrawal on one date against one bank account), not a document composed of line items, so this follows the same structural family as `ProductBatch`/`ReorderLevel` rather than the header+items shape used by Journal Entries/Sales/Purchase documents.
- **`finance_bank_account_id` is required, `cascadeOnDelete`** — a transaction has no meaning without the bank account it belongs to, same reasoning as every required parent-owns-child FK in this project; verified in testing that deleting a `FinanceBankAccount` correctly cascades away its transactions.
- **`journal_entry_id` is optional, `nullOnDelete`** — a bank transaction can optionally be tied to the `JournalEntry` that recorded its accounting-side posting (e.g. a deposit recorded here can point at the GL entry that debited the bank's Chart of Accounts line and credited a revenue account), but is not required to have one — many real transactions (e.g. a raw bank feed import, before Bank Reconciliation exists to match it against anything) won't have a corresponding journal entry yet. This is independent from, not a replacement for, `FinanceBankAccount.chart_of_account_id`'s own optional GL link built in the previous session — the bank account links to its GL *account*, while a transaction can separately link to the specific GL *entry* that posted it.
- **`reconciled` (boolean) and `reconciled_date` (nullable date) are added now, proactively**, anticipating the very next roadmap module (Bank Reconciliation) the same way `is_group` was added to Chart of Accounts ahead of Journal Entries actually enforcing it. For this task, they're plain manually-togglable fields on the create/edit form (no dedicated "mark reconciled" endpoint, no matching-against-a-bank-statement logic) — Bank Reconciliation, when built, will presumably add the real comparison workflow and may retrofit a dedicated action, following the "build the dependency, then retrofit" pattern already used repeatedly in this project, rather than building speculative reconciliation logic here.
- `transaction_type` is a simple 2-value enum (`deposit`/`withdrawal`) — deliberately not reusing Journal Entries' debit/credit vocabulary, since a bank transaction is described in the bank's own everyday terms, matching Cash Book's Receipts/Payments relabeling precedent from two sessions ago (a deposit is conceptually a receipt, a withdrawal a payment, from the bank account's point of view).
- No running-balance computation was added here — this module is pure data capture (like Stock Entry/Opening Stock in Inventory before Inventory Transactions existed to compute a live balance); a future Bank Reconciliation or a Cash Book extension could aggregate these transactions into a running balance, but that's explicitly out of scope for this data-entry module.

### 2026-08-04 (8)

Completed

- Bank Reconciliation (eighth Accounting module — matches a bank statement's opening/closing balance against the recorded `BankTransaction`s for that account, marking each matched transaction reconciled)

Scope decision

- Inspected `BankTransaction` directly before starting — it already carries `reconciled`/`reconciled_date` columns, added proactively in the prior session specifically anticipating this module ("Bank Reconciliation, when built, will presumably add the real comparison workflow"). This module is exactly that comparison workflow, not a new parallel data model.
- **Header + membership-only items, not header + priced items** — `bank_reconciliation_items` has just `bank_transaction_id`, no quantity/price/condition fields, since a reconciliation line doesn't add new data of its own; it just claims an existing `BankTransaction` row into this reconciliation session. This is the first master-detail table in this project where the "item" is a pure foreign-key membership record with zero own attributes beyond the two FKs.
- **New integration logic, not present in any prior master-detail service**: `BankReconciliationService::syncItems()` doesn't just delete-then-recreate the join rows — it also flips the referenced `BankTransaction.reconciled` flag: transactions newly included are marked `reconciled = true` with `reconciled_date` set to the statement date; transactions previously included but removed from the new submission are unmarked back to `reconciled = false` / `reconciled_date = null`. `delete()` on the whole reconciliation similarly unmarks every transaction it had claimed before removing the header. This is the same "one module's service reaches into another module's table to update a status flag" pattern already established by `SupplierQuotationService::markRfqVendorResponded()` and `PurchaseOrderService::markSupplierQuotationSelected()`, applied here to `BankTransaction.reconciled` instead.
- **`computed_closing_balance`/`variance` are stored, server-computed columns, not accessors** — `statement_opening_balance + Σ(deposits) − Σ(withdrawals)` for every included transaction, then `variance = statement_closing_balance − computed_closing_balance`. Stored (not computed on read) because a completed reconciliation is a historical record of what was true at that point — same "snapshot, not live" reasoning already used for `SalesCommission`'s stored `sales_amount`/`commission_amount` rather than `SalesTarget`'s live-computed accessor, since a reconciliation should not silently change if the underlying `BankTransaction` rows are edited afterward.
- **`items` is a `nullable` array in the Form Request**, unlike every prior master-detail document in this project (which all require `min:1`) — a reconciliation can legitimately be saved as an empty `draft` while an admin is still in the process of matching a statement across multiple edits, so an empty item set is a valid intermediate state here, not an error.

Database

- Added `bank_reconciliations`/`bank_reconciliation_items` in one migration (`database/migrations/2026_08_04_140000_create_bank_reconciliations_table.php`):
  - `bank_reconciliations`: `reconciliation_number` unique (server-generated); `finance_bank_account_id` required `foreignId` → `finance_bank_accounts.id`, `cascadeOnDelete`; `statement_date` required date; `statement_opening_balance`/`statement_closing_balance` decimal(15,2) default 0 (the bank's own claimed figures, user-entered); `computed_closing_balance`/`variance` decimal(15,2) default 0, server-computed only (absent from the Form Request rules, same convention as every other server-computed total in this project); `reconciliation_status` enum (`draft`/`completed`/`cancelled`) default `draft`; `notes` nullable text; `status` boolean.
  - `bank_reconciliation_items`: `bank_reconciliation_id`/`bank_transaction_id` both `cascadeOnDelete`; named unique index `br_reconciliation_transaction_unique` on `(bank_reconciliation_id, bank_transaction_id)` — unlike every prior line-item table's deliberate *absence* of a uniqueness constraint (a product can appear on multiple lines of one document), the same bank transaction genuinely cannot be claimed twice by the same reconciliation, so uniqueness is enforced here.

Models

- Added `App\Models\BankReconciliation` — fillable `reconciliation_number, finance_bank_account_id, statement_date, statement_opening_balance, statement_closing_balance, computed_closing_balance, variance, reconciliation_status, notes, status`; `public const STATUSES = ['draft','completed','cancelled']`; casts `status` boolean, `statement_date` to `date`, the four money fields to `decimal:2`; relations `financeBankAccount()`, `items(): HasMany` (→ `BankReconciliationItem`); `scopeActive()`.
- Added `App\Models\BankReconciliationItem` — fillable `bank_reconciliation_id, bank_transaction_id`; relations `bankReconciliation()`, `bankTransaction()`. No casts/constants needed — the model has no attributes of its own beyond the two FKs.

Services

- Added `App\Services\BankReconciliationService` — `create()`/`update()` both compute `computed_closing_balance`/`variance` via `calculateTotals()` (described above) before writing the header, then call `syncItems()` (also described above, including the mark/unmark side effect). `delete()` unmarks every claimed transaction via a new `unmarkTransactions()` helper before removing the header (items cascade via FK, but the `BankTransaction.reconciled` flag is a separate table this project's cascade chain never reaches, so it needed an explicit unmark call here — the first place in this project where a `delete()` method does more than call `$model->delete()`).

Requests

- Added `App\Http\Requests\Admin\BankReconciliationRequest` — `finance_bank_account_id` required `exists:finance_bank_accounts,id`; `statement_date` required date; `statement_opening_balance`/`statement_closing_balance` required numeric (no `min:0`, since a statement balance can technically be negative for an overdrawn account); `reconciliation_status` required `Rule::in(BankReconciliation::STATUSES)`; `items` **nullable** array (per the Scope decision above) with `items.*.bank_transaction_id` required `distinct` `exists:bank_transactions,id`.

Controllers

- Added `App\Http\Controllers\Admin\BankReconciliationController` — index eager-loads `financeBankAccount` and `withCount('items')`; adds `finance_bank_account_id`/`reconciliation_status` AJAX filters; search matches `reconciliation_number` or the bank's `bank_name`. DataTable's `variance_formatted` column colors green when exactly `0` and red otherwise — a genuinely new "pass/fail colored figure" column for a DataTable list (every prior list's colored badges were status enums, not a computed numeric check). `create()` loads only **unreconciled** active `BankTransaction`s for the item picker (`where('reconciled', false)`), so an already-matched transaction can't accidentally be claimed by a second reconciliation; `edit()` additionally includes this reconciliation's own already-claimed transactions in that list (`orWhereIn('id', $existingTransactionIds)`) so editing doesn't silently drop the currently-selected rows from the dropdown, same "don't lose the current selection" precedent as `DebitNoteController`'s equivalent invoice-dropdown logic. `store()`/`update()`/`destroy()` all `load('items')` before logging to `ActivityLogger`, same technique as every prior master-detail module.

### 2026-08-04 (9)

Completed

- Accounts Receivable (ninth Accounting module — a read-only per-customer outstanding-balance report built directly from Sales Invoices, not from Journal Entries)

Scope decision

- Inspected `Customer`, `SalesInvoice` (its `balance_due` accessor and `STATUSES` enum), `GeneralLedgerController`, and `CashBookController` directly before starting. This module follows the exact "controller only, no new table/Model/Service/Request" shape General Ledger/Cash Book established, but reads a different source: since Sales Invoices already carry `grand_total`/`amount_paid`/`balance_due` directly, Accounts Receivable queries `SalesInvoice` rows scoped by `customer_id` rather than posting through the Chart of Accounts/Journal Entries layer the way General Ledger/Cash Book do — the same "read the originating module's own documents directly" approach Sales Reports/Purchase Reports already use elsewhere in this project, rather than routing every report through the accounting ledger.
- **No normal-balance branching needed** — unlike General Ledger's generic debit/credit-side logic, a customer's receivable balance always moves the same direction (`grand_total` increases it, `amount_paid` decreases it), so the aggregation here is simpler than General Ledger's, closer in shape to Cash Book's already-simplified version.
- **Cancelled invoices are excluded from every figure** (`invoice_status != 'cancelled'`) — a cancelled invoice was never actually billed, so it has no place in a receivable balance; same "exclude cancelled" convention already used by every prior Sales/Purchase report in this project.
- **New "overdue" concept, not present in General Ledger/Cash Book**: a per-invoice `is_overdue` flag (`balance_due > 0 && due_date` in the past) is computed on the fly for both the detail view (one flag per invoice row, shown in red) and the summary view (a per-customer overdue count column) — a genuinely new field General Ledger/Cash Book's own running-balance lines never needed, since a journal-entry line has no "due date" concept at all.
- Same two-mode single-page shape as General Ledger/Cash Book (no customer selected → summary across every customer with any invoice activity; one selected → full invoice list for that customer), with the summary additionally filtering out customers with zero invoice activity in the selected range (`->filter(fn ($row) => $row['has_activity'])`) so an unrelated customer with no invoices at all doesn't clutter the overview — a small refinement beyond General Ledger's own summary, which shows every postable account regardless of activity (there, "no activity" is itself useful information about an account that should have transactions but doesn't; here, most customers legitimately have zero invoices at any given time, so showing all of them would be noise).
- Both the summary and detail views filter on `invoice_date` for the date range (not `due_date`), matching every prior date-ranged report in this project filtering on the document's own creation/posting date, not a downstream date field.

Database

- **No new tables** — reads `sales_invoices` (built in the Sales module) directly. No Model, no Service, no Form Request, no CRUD routes.
